Peter,

**NEW YORK CITY HAS FALLEN, DAY OF MAMDANI!!**

We are in a political race for results now. I hope the Republican Party and MAGA movement can hear me on this. The stewards of capitalism must find a financial remedy to our current situation, through innovation and a commitment to sacred honor, before the nihilism and cynicism of Socialism take root. The "free market" and "free trade" must be modified for the times.

**THIS IS THE RED ALERT!** Mamdani is only the beginning. We must remain the party and movement of the working class.

| [ **FIGHT BACK AGAINST COMMUNISM** ](https://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=ce1ce9e616484205a28a45cfaf96cecf&_m=6949158710724b569a8f5279f9666f60&_e=pIQ-JDVVRY_997vChkVA5cktXD6DLZu2zyvUBncULhfDSo9TeSaWaTFO_ftQDkfE7qdvQ4vZK2NoPrbUMLYSEQMmBtwxgmgG844XcTWEyp0_ugFamuED6Qf3cQHyBmTkZ-UWy72XIUBkS6wS4HQpTBTQMXaKe6j2dtj3RyCA0tKH8WPTKdn51W97BktqE4q4Y309t686doNa9wtPxRqTZRiK7XOSbiW8RPbmlk2-89QHxX5mS8_OWZHvGsbBRW8LhTlFMFjxVsrmXJlj0DlT2et_YdiofWsCgbcaH_2YQe_4E8JFwXus-GMcVUE_O9hYJkna4KsZAOU09Y1I2P2mIbM0Bn2ZPk8fs67opmSgZ098SV1XFStqyGdpA1c_sW1PkuXbnHB_wt-7U66YbVmrnInPe3tJlEeUeTLjbO6Xfj22akHbw5S2ty1RRmb0lpSyzvZmMdDxCjQqIe9cqDXM5Hb7Wi8D7g96XvKkbHWyG2kyfNiskheOGajMLBkoicB2uic0HX8VJVGf2BLZTWycLImdN5UVrwe9XEBlr0GLOmRSJMITIFmX0ZwI2UcE5yp7)

We need to deregulate, reduce taxes on the working class, and, most importantly, enforce our antitrust laws. The monopolization in America is out of control, and the monopolization of finance is abhorrent. The problem is that politicians can't say that and hope to win because the control of money controls our elections, most of the time. At this point, if we try to hold onto this way, we will have to do it by force, and inevitably, that will become destabilizing itself.

What has staved off communism in America, in the past, was the cultural belief in socioeconomic mobility. The social piece is all but blown as everyone believes they're the star in their own movie now. Everybody believes they're more important than they actually are. Which has created an inverse epidemic of self-doubt and self-hatred. The economic mobility piece must be restored. But artificial intelligence and socialism won't do it. People have to be motivated and incentivized to get better, at a craft, a passion, a job, a skill...

_If those things become invaluable, we will have an even bigger existential crisis. Who are we even as humankind?_

Still, we cannot continue to pretend like the game hasn't been rigged. It disappoints me that more Republicans don't listen to Steve Bannon when he says we have to find a way to spread this wealth around... Yes, we detest communists because we can see when and where they have waved their flag in history, genocide follows.

**The uncomfortable truth about America is at our core, we have already become a communist nation.** When we print money, bail out the failures of the rich, and socialize the risk, we have undermined capitalism and meritocracy. If your society is built on money and you socialize the money, you're a communist nation. We have to turn back now. This has to become the beating heart of the MAGA movement. We must hold the principle and move people toward the principle.

**Convenience will be the death of freedom.** If you trade your freedom for security, you deserve neither, and you will have neither. This is true for the security of basic necessities or food and welfare, as well as the security of a military-industrial complex and dollar empire.

_**THIS IS WHY THEY FEAR ME, on both sides of the aisle.**_

Meet Royce White:

**Born and raised in the Twin Cities, Royce White was the son of a single mother and started playing sports at the age of 5 years old. Living in various neighborhoods growing up, much of his family remained in the Rondo community, where he spent much of his time and received schooling. White excelled at basketball and recieved a scholarship to play basketball at the University of Minnesota, and later transferred to Iowa State. He would go on to make Dean's List while receiving All Big-12 first-team honors and many other basketball awards.

_After being selected 16th overall by The Houston Rockets in the NBA draft, White began to voice concerns about the NBA’s collective bargaining agreement (CBA), specifically regarding mental health policy, which at the time did not exist. Eventually, his concerns became a public dispute between White and the NBA. This resulted in White demanding that the NBA, as a representative of the global corporate community, take up the responsibility of spearheading the mental health conversation – not just posturing through press statements, but through policy._

Royce then went on to win two championships in Canada before moving over to play Big 3 Basketball. White appeared at a game in a t-shirt that read “Free The Uyghurs.” After a game-winning basket, White did a post-game interview on CBS, where he called for 2 Million Uyghurs to be freed and released from concentration camps. As the season went on, White would touch on taboo topics such as Gain of Function Research, The Federal Reserve, Julian Assange, Edward Snowden, Larry Hoover, Jeff Fort, Muammar Gaddafi, The Great Reset, Ivermectin, Me Too, etc.

Now, Royce White is running for Senate in Minnesota to take down the Radical Left. Republicans have not seen recent success in Minnesota, but Royce's campaign is different: a grassroots movement that's sick of the Radical Agenda pushed by Far Left Democrats Tina Smith and Ilhan Omar. Royce needs your help to pull off a fourth quarter comeback victory and FLIP Minnesota Red for Republicans.

body:
The GOP has a 53-47 majority in the Senate. THIS is how we will restore Democratic control...
#
Here's some quick math, Peter.
**Republicans currently hold a 53-47 majority in the U.S. Senate.**
**Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take control.**
That might sound like a lot. But look at the map right now:
We’re already favored to flip **North Carolina** – an open seat currently held by the GOP. **Maine** and **Ohio** are both GOP-held seats rated as TOSS-UPS.
That’s three seats we feel pretty good about.
And we haven’t even mentioned **Alaska** , **Iowa** , or **Texas** – states that are suddenly, shockingly in play for 2026.
**[FLIP THE SENATE: CHIP IN NOW](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/107374?refcode=em20260808-10778&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=10778%2E614464%2Eoj0O5I)**
**_Cook Political Report_ recently shifted FOUR Senate ratings in Democrats' direction, calling the likeliest outcome a one-to-three seat Democratic pickup – and noting that four seats, a full majority, is within reach.**
The environment is ripe. We’ve got strong candidates running in each of these races. Now, the only thing we need is the resources to compete in every single one of these races and MORE.
November will be here before we know it. That’s why we need your help:
**[So PLEASE, Peter, will you chip in $15 or more today to fund our fight to flip all of these seats and more across the country this year?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/107374?refcode=em20260808-10778&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=10778%2E614464%2Eoj0O5I)**

clean_body: | Peter, After the sudden death of my brother, Lindsey Graham, I was appointed by Governor Henry McMaster to represent South Carolina in the United States Senate. President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's "Complete and Total Endorsement," I'm running to represent South Carolina for a full term in the United States Senate. I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, but I am ready. I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge. It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times. I am not Lindsey. I have my own way of doing things. But we were raised with the same values: work hard each day, trust in the Lord, remember your roots, and never forget who you work for. I did not seek this moment, Peter. But after many prayers and speaking with my family, I know I am making the right decision to run for this seat. I'll be straight with you - I am behind financially. My opponents are self-funding millionaires or have spent years building up their campaign war chests, but I'm new to politics. We have less than 3 weeks to run against people who have been at this for years. Since you were there for Lindsey, Thank you for everything you did for Lindsey over the years. I know that having people like you in his corner meant everything to him. God bless, Darline Graham P.S. It's been a difficult week. name: Raja
subject: They chanted "Death to Krishnamoorthi"
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
I need to tell you something I don't talk about enough.
Outside of my office, a group of extremists gathered and screamed what translates to "Death to Krishnamoorthi" at the top of their lungs.
A crowd of people, in America, calling for my death.
I'm an immigrant. The son of people who came to this country with nothing because they believed it was a place where you could live freely, speak freely, and serve your community without fearing for your life. A place where disagreement didn't end in threats of violence.
Sadly, this is nothing new. I have faced this before.
A sitting Republican elected official also publicly tagged the Department of Homeland Security on social media to report me as a "foreign occupier" with an "unpronounceable name" and called for the mass deportation of Indians. I have been mocked, threatened, and told in a hundred different ways that someone like me doesn't belong in American public life.
And every single time, I have made the same choice.
Keep going.
Because the moment I stop — the moment I let the hatred win — is the moment I break faith with every family that came to this country believing it was worth fighting for. Including my own.
This is the America we are living in right now. Extremists feel emboldened to threaten, intimidate, and silence the people who are trying to do the work. Hatred has been given permission to operate in the open. The machinery of government is being used to make certain communities feel like they don't belong.
Equal Opportunity Now exists because we need leaders who have faced this kind of hatred and didn't flinch . Who know what it costs to keep going and choose to keep going anyway. Who will stand up — not just for themselves, but for every family that is being targeted, threatened, and told they don't belong.
Those leaders are out there. And they need our support right now.
Will you chip in $10, $20, or $50 to Equal Opportunity Now today to help us elect leaders who won't be intimidated — no matter what they face? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
DONATE TODAY! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
They can scream all they want.
We are not slowing down.
— Raja Krishnamoorthi
Founder | Equal Opportunity Now

Visit Our Website To Learn More! [https://www.equalopportunitynow.org/]

I’m asking you to chip in $3 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?] to help me defend one of the most competitive House seats in the country.
No, seriously. Just $3.
That’s not a typo.
I’m Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, and ever since I first won this seat in 2022, Republicans have been desperate to win it back.
They know this is one of the most competitive seats in the country – that’s why national election analysts just moved this race to "Toss-up."
They also know control of the House hinges on the outcome of our race.
That’s why the GOP and Elon Musk are preparing to spend millions on this race.
But here's the thing: I've never had billionaire donors or Washington insiders powering my campaigns. I’ve had families, workers, and small business owners – folks who just want to believe in a better future.
I’m backed by working people chipping in what they can because they want someone in Congress who understands the challenges they're facing.
That's why your $3 matters.
* $3 helps us organize communities across Southwest Washington.
* $3 helps us reach independent and working-class voters who decide elections here.
* $3 helps us fight back against the flood of outside spending and attack ads that are already on the way.
And if enough people step up, even with just a few dollars, we'll have what it takes to win one of the closest races in the country.
So I'm asking: Can you chip in $3 right now to help us defend this seat and keep fighting for working families? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]

body:
This is what we're up against
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260808-3133)
Peter,
You've heard a lot about me and my primary opponents these past few weeks. Today, I want to talk about the fight that matters most: this November.
On January 6, 2021, Congressman Tom Tiffany voted to throw out Arizona and Pennsylvania's electoral votes for president. He told reporters that day that he would have voted to reject Wisconsin's results too, if given the chance. He was the only member of Wisconsin's congressional delegation to sign onto a lawsuit trying to overturn the election results in four swing states, including ours.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260808.OsbbaN&refcode=em20260808-3133&t=1&akid=3133%2E105371%2EESYSQ4)_"I would have voted to not accept Wisconsin's results" — Tom Tiffany._
_Source: Remarks to reporters, Jan. 6, 2021 — the same day he voted to reject AZ & PA electors_
**Here's why that matters beyond 2020:** _U _nder_ Wisconsin law, the governor personally signs the certificate that certifies our state's electors for president._ The person elected governor this November will hold that pen heading into 2028.
I'm not going to sit back and breathe easy on August 11th, no matter what happens. Whether or not I'm the nominee, Wisconsin faces a race this fall against a man who's already told us he'd throw out our votes if he could.
[We're going to need a full war chest starting day one of the general election. A contribution of $10, $25, or whatever you can give today helps us make sure every Wisconsinite knows exactly who Tom Tiffany is before they vote.](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260808.OsbbaN&refcode=em20260808-3133&t=2&akid=3133%2E105371%2EESYSQ4)

With gratitude,
Fran

Is their longevity secret drinking chocolate?

---
| Untitled Document
There's an indigenous group of people called the Kuna in Panama that are a fascinating story in longevity as well as stellar cardiovascular health, and lack of metabolic diseases like Diabetes, etc.

The Kuna people drink an average of 5 cups of a type of cocoa every day and they have 9x lower rates of cardiovascular problems than the rest of the world.

High blood pressure is also almost non-existent in these people, yet they actually consume a good amount of salt.

And cancer rates are an astonishing 15x lower than the rest of the world. And they don't eat much leafy green vegetables either like most Americans try to stuff down.

They also consume a fair amount of sugar, yet their arteries are clean as a whistle, and blood sugar and blood pressure are normal and healthy.

But researchers found that it's NOT their genetics, because members who moved to cities and started eating modern processed foods suffered all the same health problems as most of the world (Diabetes, obesity, heart disease, etc).

In today's article, you'll find out the Kuna's longevity secrets, and what exact type of cocoa they drink that could be a huge part of their incredible health...

> [The Kuna drink 5 cups of a type of a cacao drink daily](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjN9AAwAAAAAAjqeu6zftsfifIG4uVf-9H770JK6ArNKFn-9U_t5xAzWL2hWRkii5JydpOTqRgs0n3gxPj0s_N8iZoYUHJzs1Zscu2-UhwjVwFTG-vWrgg) (and they have clean arteries, 9x lower heart disease rates, and healthy blood pressure and blood sugar)

This type of cacao they drink has also been shown to have up to 63x the antioxidant levels of broccoli and kale.

These particular flavanols (a type of polyphenol) in this type of cacao are shown in studies to improve heart health, lower blood pressure, boost blood flow throughout the body, improve blood sugar, and even improve your gut health by diversifying your microbiome.

Even more exciting is that the article will show you a study where cacao drinkers had nearly DOUBLE the levels of GLP-1 in their body within 2 hours of drinking cacao than people that didn't drink the cacao.

And as you know, GLP-1 in your body can help you slim down faster, so this is also a really cool benefit of drinking cacao, but strength and polyphenol levels matter as you'll see below...

[Read this article to see the type of cacao](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjN9AAwAAAAAAjqeu6zghUoxH1QaexL_0esKj_HJnFUdYBe3Zx4B4FxC6de7gJEK33yRixq6oeY4ziWrAM1J9IWv9-iK6boeO7TEPXSoOKAB13X1YKCLQg) that has all of these powerful benefits. Hint: It's NOT your average grocery store cocoa.

subject: Impact Report: Imperiled wildlife beyond the election cycle
body:
Here's what's happening at Defenders of Wildlife

Here's what's happening at Defenders of Wildlife
                  

                  

(https://support.defenders.org/s/5863521/38SyG9Xl)

(https://support.defenders.org/s/5863522/38SyG9Xl)

WILDLIFE IN THE NEWS

“The visceral, nonpartisan response to proposals to sell off federal public lands – and the widespread concern over efforts to reduce protections for national monuments – demonstrates that conservation remains a deep-seated value capable of bringing Americans together, even during this highly polarized moment.

We must build on this common ground.”

Andrew Bowman, President and CEO, on conservation of imperiled wildlife beyond the election cycle.

Read Here → (https://support.defenders.org/s/5863523/38SyG9Xl)

 

Speak Up: Tell the Federal Government Not to Weaken Wild Land Policies!

Millions of acres of wilderness-quality lands are under threat as the Department of the Interior carries out a sweeping review of wilderness policies at three land management agencies. We only have a short time to speak up and keep these lands protected for the benefit of all Americans and our wildlife! Urge the federal government not to weaken policies that protect the wildest places in national parks, refuges and more! (https://support.defenders.org/s/5863524/38SyG9Xl)

 

Birds Connect Us All to the Arctic (https://support.defenders.org/s/5863525/38SyG9Xl)

Though many of us are distant from the Arctic, this land of extremes is more connected to all of us than you may think. Millions of birds migrate from Arctic breeding grounds to wintering areas in all 50 states. Learn about the “bird highways” they travel, and more!

Read More → (https://support.defenders.org/s/5863526/38SyG9Xl)

With Wilderness Rollbacks, Wildlife Stands to Lose the Most (https://support.defenders.org/s/5863527/38SyG9Xl)

The Wilderness Act was enacted in 1964, setting up our country’s most powerful tool for protecting valuable lands and their resources. But the Trump administration is proposing changes that could open up irreplaceable wild lands to the kinds of harm that law was created to prevent – and America’s animals will suffer the most.

---
| We not only fight to safeguard fair courts and impartial judges by protecting merit-based selection systems like the one in Kansas; we wade into the rat’s nest of judicial elections and thoroughly research and vet each judicial candidate we support.

## Senate Funds Government through Midterms
The Senate voted early on Saturday to [fund the federal government until Dec. 11,](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOqzAURL_G7oiuLw6YwsVr6PLaLZHBY_DKmAicRPn7FbvFfsC2M9LRnPm4DTcXU8zzf7fClrANGa8joRTsQ4DH7tK8PbHnFbmER_bw42Ng4qYiU1E3eBfTe9DS2wAwagmrWtNwS2waudi6AxTc6K-d0QET2F_DNZDzup3GVstoTxoZ6hQpxfWlbkc1jdSYibVxxEITfCzbfvncYi4LQnqfky7Ttspkl1Luh6j_Ce4F92XBElM6O8H9sq04hQT3B7IrENw3pAxRV_0E1a9dderFPFdjTElwL3fr76-YUjyaVmiaVxe_wbL86amn5a8AAAD__6sRfcs) averting another government shutdown before the midterm elections. Lawmakers headed to summer recess [without taking up the SAVE America Act](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD3u4yAQxU9jd47GA8a4oNgmXbbd0hozQ8IK4whIotx-5b3Cv3x60vv4_bmtN4op5vtv2sW1cKxZPjVJa1LWICyF0v14S8m75BZemYW314qAZgA7wLIyxfRddc8uiKCoXtw4W4MzoDX9wymwFqegyPOivA0bayBvPHktDIB9dGcaWFhGGEdUFzVvo9_AWI_aEmCnQTi2o1z-HjG3h4T0PSdd_LH3yT1ae9ZO_erw2uGVnueB0zpFadEn6fBa6S0D7VKip4F8G6pkajIU8VLrYJiRLVgtotFMatO8zYvnyUw8TqD74vj5iSnFauZOw32nmP73tx9Bezv8FwAA__8My3-A), President Trump's proof-of-citizenship voting bill. The Senate could try to approve parts of the bill as part of a GOP package to fund the Iran war in September. The Senate also [confirmed Todd Blanche as U.S. attorney general](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO3CAURb8Gd4zwgzWmoEjjbtOmtDA8ZthgGMHzWv77yPmFra90dc7587l-upRTef52O1qKdS149oxE2NaIAZvLz_qNrexYKB4lYNiOFQRMXMxcmDW4lK9VDcFGREA5oB31PIEWME_Dy0oDUagYnQEzeSM1BNBSz2ozKjiJQ7L3m5iFGcU4gnxIvY1-E9PsQc1OAFMCQ6LaHl81FXphzNeN9PB1H7J9Eb07k78YLAyW8zwfZfO3xb0zWN41J0q-M1i-jk7JIw_4do1uIwZLx-IIua8lprZ3TjUEvmVX_Au5I6qt4MWfWO4W_ET82_lRPDZyqdDFmy_uw4zqQw_NhveZck590kyJ5-5S_k9JP0r7beFfAAAA__-rtpC4) in a mostly party-line vote, with two Republican senators, Susan Collins of Maine and Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, voting against him along with all Democrats. A separate bill to set [new rules for recruiting and compensating](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkEGu3CAMhk9DdozASQNZsOiG3eu2y8gDToaKgRF4Jpqevspre4K3sSXrs_3p__mxfmDKqew_8E6Ot7oWOnomZmrrRpEa5r2-qJU7Fd6eJVK8PldQMEtlpVrWiCm_12mIbiMCGgdy2tgZjAI7Dzc34RRD1NoapJk0LXGzo0XCMOvFmGVI7rymrFq00hrGy2iuOlzVbANMFhWISVFMXNvlV02Fb7Tl96l0CfU-ZHdjfnQxfhfgBfjjOC7Pjlwjvk9AgO9c2_vsj9q4C_Ch5kw7CfDnZwFe2f_l0SpTYPkPkX93JH6Oyt6od1mqfFUmGdrztwxY-KCcZQmIAvyiQX2bjVXKCPBDc_FxpJxTn42Y1H7HlD-9-Uthvxz8CQAA___76ZKz) college athletes was not included after Texas Sen. Ted Cruz agreed to postpone floor consideration until September.
## Wet Winter on Tap for Southern Tier of U.S.
Snow, sleet, and surprises are in store across the United States this winter, according to the _Farmers' Almanac'_ s [2026-2027 forecast](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHupCAQBvCnwQ4Do4taUFxjt9deaQYZVi4IBtgl-_YX7xX-1RSTfPl935_n9kQffHz9xpN0dWmL1EqgWilvjixlDK_0oRxPitW9oyVr3hsIUFzMXCybRR--29hZ7YiAho60nGYFk4BZdYeeHtKAUcYJ3JfloeZlMA9L06SMlCjHzus7TcxikUJKGPphMnI3Qs07jDMKYKMg62vK_d_kYz3Ihe9N6vd0dkEftV6FDb8YrAzW1lrfajzuJ4P1bnMfrD5FDAxWh_mkXDiGEyPu_Mpk_V4LLzE1XgJR5RgtL-98ZV-ocJcybz5WyvyWMli7rO3VfAi-qImN4nWiD_859UcbfjT8CwAA__96Mocs). The publication expects an [active storm track](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OwyAQhU9jd1jD2MHjgmKbdNl2SwvDELPCOMIkKLdfJcoNtv309P5-LvPFhBjS9dtsrIvf58T1iFwK59mz42zidX9wThun4u_JsVvuMwIqASRgmp0J8TkPrdOeGblvWcuRFI6ApNpVk-oZrCNpB5pIytNp8qxoWKhXnvypDfrlBgSTBCmx7_pxkXYBRRYHMoDNAOxC2XP3u4dUVvbx-arU2X1ro15LuR1N_9XgucFzrbXzJm-cDxM3k4x9yRo8f6D4UPGegICjqCEVzqKyKStn4ffM1hylzdrdaogxHGpsBrhuJsR3ZvnXUQ-NfwEAAP__LgV83Q) across the southern tier, with above-normal precipitation from California through Texas, the Gulf Coast, and the Southeast. When cold air meets that moisture, storms could bring sleet, freezing rain, or heavy, wet snow. A [strengthening El Niño](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAURb_G7rDwswWkoNjGXbbd0nqBh80KQwQv8eTvR55fmP7q6Nzz777eMaaYt794kOVQ1kxnS8RMdQ3kqWLayptqPihzeGVP_vFaQYIS0gh5Wz3G9Fnn3ttABDT1ZEdtFGgJRvW7lUo6o2VwRs9AyqExiPOEk8JZ3XToo71o0sjbKMcRpmHSj9E9pDIOZoMSulmSj1zq8L_EzDuF9LmUBleOPtmd-dm66U8HSwfLeZ5DLojDVt4dLNcbUSkRNupgoSRyzEWEUo8m6OtJjskLLqJxpbzxTlk0_IgLca3IYWOqra_WP8-YUmxKd7PcDozpR4B_Ve1t4TsAAP__lTyDUQ), marked by unusually warm tropical Pacific waters, is expected to drive the wet pattern. The northern tier can expect near-normal temperatures, while inland Northeast cities may see heavy, wet snow, especially in January and February.
## Million-Dollar Homes Go Mainstream
Nearly 7 million U.S. homes are now [worth at least $1 million](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGypCAQRb8GM6y2dZUJCDYxm003tEBaZauBKcBx5-9f-X7h5ffce-v8fS5P49nH_Y8JpOuWlkhXYaqV8rKRo2x4T2_KMVCs2xkdOXsuCDhKUBIeizOeP8vQOL0RIfUN6W5SI06AamwObQGHdbUwAjmwZvhlJgXKuU6RUsqtjdd3Gyh4dNB12Lf9ZLsbUCsOygCKAcj5mnL7L_lYD9r4c19q1xQa1ketryL63wJngfN1Xe2W_tuz-Eil3BmBcybDkko1lQTOwTP7FKVLzCbLIwWSltYUfNxlOfMr--Ljzh8ZUw6Gm6zd67qhMk5igD0Yz9_r9UfK3hq_AgAA___zRINV), up from about 1.5 million in 2005, according to the National Association of Realtors. Those properties make up 8% of the market, and in Hawaii, roughly 40% of homes have crossed that threshold. Meanwhile, Americans need to earn about $110,000 a year to afford even a typical home, a Redfin report found. The median household income sits at roughly $88,000, leaving a [gap of more than $22,000](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGypiAMhZ8GO5wQFbGg2IbubrulgxJ-2UFwEK_j2-94X2GbpEjmnO-cP1_zlw0xpM9vu5OuPs-J7jNSrVRmT46KjZ_8TSXtlKq_kiO3XDMCSg6KwzQ7G-Iz943Tngipa0iLUUkcAZVsNm37xdEkJjGQWsB3cvWT7WH0Uoy290MT9KsGCiYBQmDXduMi1gWkWrFXFpD1QC7UXNq_OaS6kY_Pi9SueW-i3mo9Ttb9YmgYmvu-2-u0NTv7vA8MzVlzeRiaPSd692vH0IB6x8DQhLTmnXgicuS49T4Xx-tzhNVGfp18e68_kQs5HxIvdORSGZpJCDUoOQGMDE1TtDvuEGM45ch6-Ow2xB_K-l_Vfmv8FwAA__-jSIqf) between what families earn and what it takes to buy. The affordability squeeze has eased slightly, with the gap shrinking from $26,000 a year ago and $29,000 two years ago as [incomes rise faster than housing costs](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uwyAURp8Gb1hwcTAZGLp4S9eOFoZLTMVPBCSu375KX6H7p-8cna_bejMhhnz_NAl192XNeLSIvWNdPTqsJt7LC2tOmLt_Zodue67AQFKmKLuuzoR4rtPgtEcEFANqPisJMwMlh11b8MYxmA1KCRc5KWB8E0ZcxNXzzbkh6PcbU-zKGecgRjFv3G5MKguTMgzIxNCFXur4XULuO_p4vpVGW9IQ9d77oxHxQWAhsBzHMfrysz1byNjae0NgQVtySSeBZceKjYZsS0KaER06arwv1dF-PoI1kZqENViT6V4SDlW7xxFiDE3OZGL3ZEL8I_d_5Xpp-A0AAP__ROSA5A). Redfin defines "affordable" as a buyer's mortgage not consuming more than 30% of their income.

## Texas Officer Jailed in Mexico Killings
Mexican authorities [arrested Santa Anna reserve police](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkbHunDAMh58mbD6FcAVuYOjC9u_aERnHHG5DghLfwb19RfsIXSzrs2Tr8-_n1_SFEiQ-f-DGg55LmiIfJbAq50nPtCxCnH-hBPYSNz6FEuXJWdeC7cE-JiSVN093rPwwW_-oKx7qrm9d1zTto1oHtITobdthN7c4d99sV7fs29o3nZuJKxmudba3j7q27t7f5p76hpm9o7lpuDF3y1405ZuurHxiWcInvTnfKG1VGFbVvZjmu3GjceNxHLffBfUaGjdePsaNFwGJby4qT1S-2HXWuNH2V7m6zHvKCkvKG2eY-cQMlF5RP7BnJomk4MDz_tIPUIpFcQ4MSPQq7CEtoFn2wLCmTUg8g0T49zRYArPEJ2iCV4FDdIWSonFjlQe_HxKClLYzd_vcUMJfM_3fRN6D-xMAAP__74mlHQ) officer Chad Eberle at the border Tuesday, hours after a shooting in Saltillo left three people dead. Eberle, 35, had gone to a home in the Coahuila capital to take custody of his 3-year-old son without permission, according to the Mexican newspaper _La Raz on_. Two women and a man were killed, and the boy's mother was critically wounded. Eberle drove north with the boy and was stopped at International Bridge II in Piedras Negras, across the river from Eagle Pass. He faces homicide charges and is held at the Saltillo Men's Penitentiary. Police Chief Ryan Tucker said the arrest "was a shock" and that Eberle is on unpaid administrative leave. State licensing records show he [previously worked](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1urDAUBOCnMZ2RsVkwhYvb0O1tU6KDfYAT-QcZ78K-fbRJ3iD9aDTzfdynO5CnuP6HgKZcS5oinofHUjBP5UrLQhbzJ5BHRzHgRTbZPEkhOy40F8MEttATpxYqZ2bhhqZC0_S6k71S3VBtBgXcpJ57rebb0A8gcZhxaRws7a2xbVeRedcJLYamEbLV9aytVojopJ2VQsVagY5KynXZsOAFx-Jf6Ym5tilU3myl7AdT_5gcmRzP86xnWm16xJJfWwq4w4rvKJOjzRSQyfGAWIBDjMD35Mki_73KwdrHgY6nhZdMu0e-pUCWHHKK_EeAybHKxu0neU9H17NWrAHIf-8pf3V8GvkVAAD__yuVjBE) for the Bexar County Precinct 2 constable's office, Northside ISD, and the Somerset and Bangs police departments.
## Cruz Bill Stalls Before Senate Recess
A handful of senators objected Friday to a quick vote on [Sen. Ted Cruz's college sports bill](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLFypDAQRL8GMlFC4lgRKLiEbC-9kBqkEYwtECXNLvjvXfgXHHd1d733_zk9gSLtyz_Y0PIV0rTjWSIyY574SiGQw_wBFNHTvuFFLrk8Kal6IY2QwwSO6Y1TB7W3s_RDW6NtH6ZXD637oV6tUi7AHMDpYFqEPyGAB1ReS9carXVN9p6TRg5tK1Vnmtk4oxHRKzdrjbrqJHrilBtekfGCEuJXemNuXNrqaFfmo1T6b6XGSo3neTafXLY7rNR481RqdClGXFCUI2UuYqYYxZqip30Rr0MU3IGxiAN4FZwEvJZXYZHRYbnrdbb-OClGKv2j6uSyAcWfe_6ttrdV3wEAAP__t-CGbQ), threatening to push the measure to September. The [Protect College Sports Act](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1uhSAYxvGrwU3DVxAGhi5up2tHg_CiNCgn8Ebt3Tdt2is48y95nuT_8ZgfLuV0rO9uB4t3LPMBV8uACHXGu8SYPNRPlzKEdOxwJ198nTnlqqe6p2Z2HtMJs3RdsAsNhnVg2agVH4VQptusYBKCYSDHJURhlAQWdFSjN15RJmOX7M8c1dQwRrnUw6K9FgAQuF-EAEEkhZCw1AE3QLhdi_mrnFAHX_Yu2w3x2Yh4I3wifLqua_DlWCu0NqzlJHxaUs6ET4wZ3Pp_I3xqcDiE_o-lUrqrNjyvlHNqaiSSrrtL-fcGX81zWv4dAAD__586eq8), co-authored by Cruz and Sen. Maria Cantwell, D-Washington, would close a loophole that let booster collectives route endorsement money around the $21.3 million cap schools use to pay athletes directly. The bill gained momentum last week when the SEC and Big Ten [dropped their opposition](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OnTAUBOCnMZ2vzDELpnCRxt2mTYn8c4ATGRvZDrBvH910qbcezafR_PpcPi1FSttPe6Buz5qXhHeN2BqWpT15Xclj-W0pYqB04EM--7KAgJELxcW8WN_owmWwXdBOhLnvUPeTGmGScpy7XctZzUIJ5QTAJMG5QXolnQRnbQhu7Ei_OaHE3PcCBvVyyiuJiAG8kxIlGwQGarm82o4NH1vX-JUvLC-fjy7qvbWzMvmDgWFg7vt-YT3TO2RgfI4RN-T1zKVVBqa2XL4YmIWBocDADPOH6KcPYGAcbbxh4hU9r3_Od4X_D3BHMfKCF12UNl4x2Ybc7zZ5rF3R4bwpRqrjxAaxHZbiv5Htu-deGv4GAAD__6jNkRs) after negotiators added a $27.5 million retention and Olympic sports pool. _"We listened to our colleagues, addressed their concerns, and improved an already strong bill,"_ Cruz said. Not every Texan is sold. The chairs of the University of Texas and Texas A&M regent boards wrote Cruz and Sen. John Cornyn in June opposing an earlier draft, and Sen. Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

| | **While Everyone Watches Hormuz, a Second Chokepoint Has Quietly Cut Saudi Crude Flows in Half. Here Is Why the Bab al-Mandeb Keeps Your Energy Costs Elevated Even If Hormuz Reopens.**
---
| | Lost in the week’s focus on the Strait of Hormuz is a second maritime chokepoint that has become a structural driver of oil prices: the Bab al-Mandeb, the narrow strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa. Shipping tracker Kpler reported that since the Houthis began targeting Saudi shipping on July 22, average Saudi crude flows through the Bab al-Mandeb have fallen 50%. **This matters enormously because the Bab al-Mandeb became the primary alternative route for Saudi crude exports to Asia precisely because of the disruptions in Hormuz.** With both chokepoints compromised, Saudi Arabia is forced onto the long route around the Cape of Good Hope, adding roughly 15 days to each voyage.
---
| | The economics are directly inflationary and they reach your household. Taking the long route around Africa adds around 15 days to the journey — meaning higher fuel consumption, fatter crew bills, increased insurance premiums, and fewer voyages each tanker can complete. Every one of those costs is passed through to the delivered price of crude, and ultimately to the price you pay for gasoline and heating. **For the August 14 CPI and beyond, the Bab al-Mandeb disruption is why the energy premium may prove stickier than a Hormuz reopening alone would suggest.** Even if Hormuz reopens through the blockade-for-transit framework, the Houthi threat to the Bab al-Mandeb remains a separate, unresolved problem. Full normalization of Saudi export economics requires both chokepoints secure — and the Houthi situation shows no sign of resolution. This is why the realistic base case for oil is elevated, not a return to pre-war levels.
---
| | Sources: CNN / Kpler, August 2, 2026 · CNBC, August 7, 2026 · Trading Economics, August 7, 2026

Even if Hormuz reopens through the blockade-for-transit framework, the Houthi threat to the Bab al-Mandeb remains a separate, unresolved problem. Full normalization of Saudi export economics requires both chokepoints secure — and the Houthi situation shows no sign of resolution. #
Friend, I’ve got to be honest: this is one of the toughest times of the year for a grassroots campaign like ours. People are soaking up the last few rays of summer sunshine, school is just around the corner, and families are spending extra quality time with each other before things get busy. I’m all in favor of it – but that also means that campaign donations tend to slow down. **This is what we call the summer slump – the dreaded time where donations take a dip, and grassroots campaigns like ours begin to _really_ feel the pinch. ** It happens every cycle – but this time is a bit different. With MI-08 being named “Seat 218” – the seat that could decide who controls Congress, every moment matters. Not an exaggeration! **We simply can’t afford to slow down – not when National Republicans have already committed to spending over $2.5 million. ** And that’s only the beginning, friend. clean_body: | Friend, I’ve got to be honest: this is one of the toughest times of the year for a grassroots campaign like ours. People are soaking up the last few rays of summer sunshine, school is just around the corner, and families are spending extra quality time with each other before things get busy. I’m all in favor of it – but that also means that campaign donations tend to slow down. This is what we call the summer slump – the dreaded time where donations take a dip, and grassroots campaigns like ours begin to really feel the pinch. It happens every cycle – but this time is a bit different. With MI-08 being named “Seat 218” – the seat that could decide who controls Congress, every moment matters. Not an exaggeration! We simply can’t afford to slow down – not when National Republicans have already committed to spending over $2.5 million. And that’s only the beginning, friend. Midterm races are decided by turnout margins that would look like rounding errors in a presidential race. Our ballot-chasers are in those districts **right now.**

**Tyler Bowyer**

As permitted by law, TPPAC, Inc. maintains a non-contribution account for the purpose of influencing federal, state, and local elections. Federal law requires us to use our best efforts to collect and report the name, address, occupation, and employer of individuals whose contribution exceeds $200 in an election cycle. It's the story of a modern-day Daniel--the kind of story you'd expect to read about in history books, not the news. Daniel Grand is an Orthodox Jew. As a faithful practitioner of his faith, he simply wanted to host a small prayer gathering in his home with about a dozen friends. But a neighbor learned about Daniel's plans and reported him to the mayor, demanding that the city "put a stop to this." Shockingly, University Heights, Ohio did exactly that. City officials ordered Daniel to obtain a permit to hold the prayer gathering in his home, classifying it as a "place of religious assembly." Then things got worse. To make sure Daniel didn't hold prayer meetings without the permit, the city began surveilling his home and even encouraged neighbors to spy on him and report any suspected violations. Daniel tried to comply. But there was an impossible catch. The permit process wasn't designed for a family home--it was designed for churches, synagogues, and other dedicated houses of worship. If he successfully obtained the permit, Daniel and his family would have to stop living in their own house. In other words, the city presented him with an impossible choice: abandon his proposed prayer meetings or give up his house. And when Daniel filed a lawsuit seeking to rectify this violation of this free-exercise rights, the federal courts told him he needed to complete the permitting process first. _By Eric J. Lullove, DPM, CWSP, MAPWCA, FFPM RCPS(Glasg)_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f37be0c8-fca6-4d63-a3f4-1b0aaac99e3a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
There is a particular kind of policy violence that never makes the evening news. It doesn't arrive as a headline or a hearing. It arrives as a payment formula, published in the middle of July, in a document thousands of pages long, written in language specifically designed so that no ordinary person -- and almost no busy physician -- will ever read it. And then, if we say nothing, it becomes law by default.
That is exactly what is happening right now with the CY 2027 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule.
I've written before about what this proposed rule does to physicians. Today I want to write about what it does to _patients_ -- because that is the part CMS is counting on you to overlook, and it is the part that should make every one of us pick up a pen.
## **What the rule actually does**
On July 14, 2026, CMS released its proposed rule for how it will pay physicians in 2027.1 Buried inside is a change to something called Modifier -25. In plain English: when a doctor addresses a separately identifiable problem _and_ performs a procedure on the same day, the current system pays for both. Under the proposal, the most expensive service that day gets paid at 100 percent -- and every other service gets paid at 50 percent.2 Half. CMS is specifically proposing to cut payment when a physician handles a same-day office visit alongside a procedure that carries a global surgical period.3
CMS calls this eliminating "duplicative" payment. I call it what it is: a financial penalty for taking care of complicated patients in a single visit.
And here is the quiet part said out loud. This penalty does not fall evenly. CMS's own analysis expects a large negative impact on dermatology, otolaryngology, and podiatry, while most other specialties actually see a small _increase_ as those dollars get redistributed to them.4 The money doesn't disappear. It gets moved -- away from the specialties that manage skin, wounds, feet, and chronic complexity, and toward specialties that don't.
## **Now think about whose care this is**
This is the part I need you to sit with, because the abstraction hides the cruelty.
Who are the patients who show up with two problems on the same day? They are not the healthy. They are the diabetic on dialysis whose foot ulcer needs debridement _and_ whose new pressure wound needs evaluation. They are the elderly, the neuropathic, the vascularly compromised, the medically fragile -- the people for whom a single appointment already takes real effort to reach, and for whom being told "come back another day for the second problem" isn't a scheduling note. It's a barrier that ends in an infection, a hospitalization, an amputation.
When you cut the second same-day service to half payment, you don't cut a line item. You create an incentive to send that patient home with one problem unaddressed. The system will quietly reward doing less for the people who need the most. The patients with the hardest, most complex, most expensive-to-manage conditions are precisely the ones this rule makes least worth treating in full.
Let me say that as plainly as I can: **this proposal will hurt the sickest Medicare beneficiaries in America, and it will hurt them most where their problems are most complex.** That is not a side effect. It is the mathematical center of the policy.
**Before you read further:** The comment period on this rule closes September 14, 2026. [Anyone can file one at regulations.gov](https://substack.com/redirect/532d881d-d4c6-4034-93b9-124c906cf776?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), **file code CMS-1848-P.**
It takes five minutes and you do not need to be an expert. The Capitol switchboard is (202) 224-3121.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.2OLv1wzK3PBn9OaB942_PbdtZreR7kaErBrKCccdYsk?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=210274892)
> Dr. Eric Lullove treats the patients this rule is about--the diabetic on dialysis, the neuropathic foot, the wound that turns into an amputation if it waits two weeks for a second appointment. He read the CY 2027 fee schedule so you don't have to, and he found the line where CMS quietly decided that the second problem you bring to a doctor is worth half as much as the first.

What's behind the wall is the harder half: why a payment formula that punishes complexity fits a pattern this administration keeps repeating, and how a system that gives hospitals an inflation raise every year while cutting physician pay for two decades isn't broken so much as built.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260809_1.T1pHma&refcode=em20260809-1&t=1003&akid=8206%2E582294%2Ewb0b6- ]Before I dive into the highlights of this article from The
Atlantic...Iowa’s U.S. Senate election could decide who takes the Senate
majority in November. Will you split a donation of $10 or $15 between my
campaign and Chris Pappas to help us fight back against MAGA and take back
control of our country?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260809_1.T1pHma&refcode=em20260809-1&t=1004&akid=8206%2E582294%2Ewb0b6- ]Split a donation »

Below is an excerpt from The Atlantic:

There are a few ways to think about Iowa. You might imagine America’s 29th state
as the land of corn and pigs (20 million hogs can’t be wrong, reads my favorite
T-shirt for sale at the Eastern Iowa Airport). Maybe you associate it with Field
of Dreams, Caitlin Clark, or the future birthplace of Captain James T. Kirk.

You might also picture Iowa as flat, like a pancake. But you would be wrong.
Iowa is not even in the top five flattest U.S. states, which is a fact I was
considering last month as I watched Josh Turek size up a daunting set of stairs
in a hilly Cedar Rapids neighborhood. After a moment’s consideration, the
47-year-old Democrat, who uses a wheelchair, shook his head, deciding against
it. It would be the only house that Turek would skip that afternoon as he
knocked on doors in the warm spring sunlight. At all the other homes, he
followed the same elaborate routine without appearing to break a sweat: lowering
his body out of his chair and onto the ground; hoisting himself backwards up a
step using just his arms; yanking the wheelchair up after him; and repeating
that until he reached the doorbell, which is when he would announce, “Hi! I’m
Josh Turek, and I’m running for the U.S. Senate!”

In his bid to replace Republican Senator Joni Ernst, Turek is hoping to correct
what he believes is another popular misconception about Iowa: that it is a red
state.

All across Iowa’s 99 counties, people keep telling me that they feel more
hopeful than they have in a decade or more.

I feel the same way.

And it isn’t just happening in Iowa. This sentiment is shared by millions
of working people all across this country.

This is a once-in-a-generation opportunity. The stars are aligning in our
favor. Trump won Iowa by 13 points in 2024, now it’s TIED in multiple
polls.

Experts, pundits, and even our opponents know this is unlike any election
in recent history.

My Trump-endorsed opponent is backed up by $50 million in dark money.
Chris Pappas and I need your urgent support to keep our TV ads, digital
ads, get-out-the-vote tour, door-knocking, phone banking, voter
registration, and so much more, going through the fall.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260809_1.T1pHma&refcode=em20260809-1&t=1005&akid=8206%2E582294%2Ewb0b6- ]Will you split a donation of $10, $15, or more to help Chris Pappas and
me seize this opportunity to flip Iowa, take back the Senate, and change
this country?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260809_1.T1pHma&amount=5&refcode=em20260809-1&t=1024&akid=8206%2E582294%2Ewb0b6- ]Donate $5 »

— Josh Turek

Team:
We are more than halfway through 2026, and the statistics from the Gun Violence Archive are terrifying:
* **7,500** gun-involved deaths
* **14,000** gun-involved injuries
* **250** mass shootings
* **300** children shot or killed
* **2,000** teenagers shot or killed

This is not normal. This is not okay. When will enough be enough?

We’ve seen tragedy after tragedy, yet too many lawmakers refuse to acknowledge our national gun violence crisis, or take action to address it. We are not safe at home, school, church, or picking up a bite to eat.
To make matters worse, Donald Trump wants handguns to be delivered through the United States Postal Service. This would severely undermine a law that has been in place for almost 100 years! This move would seriously endanger public safety, lead to an increase in gun-related violence, and make law enforcement’s job to track weapons even more difficult.
[**GIFFORDS is on the front lines to stop the gun violence epidemic. And with less than 100 days until the election, we need your donations to help defeat extremist politicians who would put the NRA before our families and win back a gun sense majority.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260809-1-b&t=2&akid=11708%2E3935704%2E8w0GKY)

The Washington Post is calling our race “highly competitive,” and I need your immediate grassroots support to keep the momentum.
#
Peter, look at this:
[](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/106994?refcode=em20260809-10779&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=10779%2E614464%2EDfPVtc)
Ohio is the most competitive race in the country – and analysts agree. The Republican dark money machine sees it too, and they’re funneling a whopping $133 million to drown us out before Ohio voters even get a say.
**[Please, will you split $15 between me and State Democrats Committee?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/106994?refcode=em20260809-10779&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=15&t=2&akid=10779%2E614464%2EDfPVtc)**
The political ground in Ohio is shifting, and voters are taking a harder look at the direction things are headed. That means the seat Husted was appointed to – never elected to – is winnable.
That’s why this race is already on track to be one of the most expensive Senate races in history – if we don’t win Ohio, we can’t flip the Senate blue. With the latest poll from _The New York Times_ showing me within striking distance of Husted, the avalanche of Republican money could be enough to bury our momentum for good if we don’t respond right now.
I can’t win this race alone. **[Please, will you split $15 or more now to help me and State Democrats Committee fight back, flip this seat, and keep Ohio in play?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/106994?refcode=em20260809-10779&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=15&t=3&akid=10779%2E614464%2EDfPVtc)**
Thank you.
–Sherrod

Peter - I'm not a politician. In fact, I've never run for office before.

I never expected to be running for office. I have never had any desire to be a politician. I am doing this because I am answering President Donald Trump's call to serve and want to stand up for South Carolina and fight for his agenda.

_**Like Lindsey, I am a hard worker with a servant's heart.**_ We grew up in the back of a bar and liquor store, in one room. Our parents worked hard every day to make ends meet - there was no time for sickness and few vacations, because if the doors weren't open, no money was coming in.

What I've spent my life doing is serving South Carolina - including running a state agency with 130 employees and a $90 million budget. We turned it from a struggling organization into a national model helping people find work and live independently. We made sure all spending was reasonable, allowable, and necessary. _I fought against duplication of services, knowing it wasted taxpayers' dollars_.

| | | | | On August 18th, a law takes effect that kills tax credits for every new solar and wind project in America.

Every single one.

But one energy source keeps full government backing for eight more years.

It runs 24 hours a day.

Zero carbon. Zero fuel costs.

It doesn’t care if the sun sets or the wind stops.

Google just signed a 15-year contract for it..

Bill Gates reversed a decade-old position and wrote a $100 million check.

The company at the center has been building this technology for sixty years.

| | **The Summer’s Single Most Important Number Arrives Thursday: the July CPI, Five Days Away. Here Is the Base Case, the Risks, and Why You Should Position for a Balanced Coin-Flip.**
---
| | The week of August 10 delivers the single most important data release of the summer: the July CPI on Thursday, August 14, now five days away. Everything the market processed over the volatile past two weeks — the interim proposal, the Geneva postponement, the restrictive draft, the blockade-for-transit framework, the 7% weekly Brent decline — funnels into that Thursday morning print. **With Brent having closed down more than 7% but still elevated in the high $70s to low $80s, the July monthly average points toward a CPI headline near 3.8%, the middle of the base case.** That would keep the September 16 Fed decision genuinely contested rather than resolving it in either direction.
---
| | For your portfolio, the balanced coin-flip counsels against a directional bet. **An investor who positions heavily for a hold — piling into rate-sensitive REITs and long-duration bonds — risks a hawkish CPI surprise. An investor who positions heavily for a hike — dumping all rate-sensitive holdings — risks a dovish surprise that sparks a relief rally.** The balanced position, the one the earnings season validated, is to hold capital-light and direct-conversion AI names that perform in either scenario, manage rate-sensitive holdings to a neutral weight, and keep the intermediate AI tier light until the September 2 Micron result. The largest risk to the 3.8% base case is a fresh supply shock pushing it toward 3.9–4.0%; the largest disinflationary surprise is a signed deal breaking Brent below $75 and pulling it toward 3.7%.

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Amazon received $600 million from the government. Apple got $2.2 billion. Walmart received $2.4 billion.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2986%2E4032634%2EoB_TlF)
---
Donald Trump illegally imposed tariffs on the American people — and they deserve to get their money back. The Supreme Court ruled that the chaotic tariffs he put in place last year — tariffs that drove up prices and led many companies to raise prices and cost the average family an estimated $2,500 — were illegal. The government is now supposed to return $166 billion in illegally collected tariffs. **Woo-hoo, justice was served! Right?** Well, instead of putting that money back in the hands of the people who paid the price, big corporations are recouping the funds. Amazon has received $600 million from the government. Apple? They got $2.2 billion. Walmart received $2.4 billion. The list goes on. The result? Trump's illegal tariffs gave large corporations two big wins: First when they passed those tariff costs along to consumers, and now again through a refund back to the corporations. And working families who paid higher prices are left without a clear way to recover those costs. **That’s why I’m pressing for companies like Apple, Amazon, Walmart, Nike, Target, and others to give the refunds they are receiving directly to consumers.** [**Add your name to keep up the pressure: The American people bore the costs for these illegal tariffs, and these big corporations need to pass these refunds back to consumers.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-tariff-refunds/?source=EW_EMZ32U_DEM_FUN_20260809_F&refcode=EW_EMZ32U_DEM_FUN_20260809_F&t=8&akid=2986%2E4032634%2EoB_TlF) | [**ADD YOUR NAME**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-tariff-refunds/?source=EW_EMZ32U_DEM_FUN_20260809_F&refcode=EW_EMZ32U_DEM_FUN_20260809_F&t=9&akid=2986%2E4032634%2EoB_TlF)

subject: Here’s an inside look at how Abdul beat $70 million
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U

Hey Peter,

I wrote the memo below for our own team after winning the Democratic
primary. I wasn’t planning to share this out wide, but you were a major
factor in helping us pull off this win. So you should read it too.

Before you do, I need to tell you something: Mike Rogers has a year-long
head start and tens of millions of dollars backing his campaign to defeat
us. [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260809-1-ak._EKcU5&amount=10&refcode=em20260809-2871&t=1004&akid=2882%2E251025%2EXIjVgD ]Can you chip in $10 or any amount right now to help
us start closing that gap?

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260809-1-ak._EKcU5&amount=10&refcode=em20260809-2871&t=1005&akid=2882%2E251025%2EXIjVgD ]Donate $10 ››

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

TO: Interested Parties
FR: Alia K., Abdul for U.S. Senate Campaign Manager
RE: How We Beat $70 Million

Last night, a man named Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, who swore off corporate PAC
money and went toe-to-toe with the political establishment, beat $70
million in outside spending to win a primary election in Michigan.

Abdul began this race in third place.

Abdul was outspent 10:1.

No Democratic primary candidate for U.S. Senate has ever withstood this
much big money and won. Until now.

We built a working class movement of Michiganders united around the
promise of “Money out of Politics, Money in Your Pocket, and Medicare for
All.”

This is how we did it — and what it means for the general election:

A NEW KIND OF DEMOCRATIC COALITION
You are not supposed to overcome $70 million in outside spending — let
alone $70 million plus the full weight of the Washington establishment.

We did it by assembling a broad coalition that drove record turnout. More
than 1.5 million Michiganders voted in this Democratic primary, the
highest ever in a non-presidential year. More Michiganders voted for Abdul
(741k) than voted for Senator Elissa Slotkin in her 2024 primary (713k) or
Governor Gretchen Whitmer (588k) in her 2018 primary. And while more than
1.5 million Democrats turned out to vote in this election, only 807,000
Republicans did. So far, Abdul has won more than 20 counties that voted
for Trump in the 2024 presidential election, and he’s currently winning
the counties that were competitive in the 2024 presidential election by 8
points. Some of Abdul’s greatest victories were in the media markets where
our spending gap was widest. In Marquette and South Bend markets, where we
couldn’t spend a dime on TV, we won 9 out of 11 counties. In Lansing,
where we were outspent 43:1, we won 3 out of 5 counties. Taken together,
Abdul’s ability to build a coalition that overcame an impossible 11:1
spending disadvantage shows exactly the kind of durable strength a general
election candidate needs.

A TRUSTED MESSENGER
Michiganders know and like Abdul. To residents of Detroit and Wayne
County, he’s the Health Commissioner who got free eyeglasses for children
who needed them and cancelled medical debt for thousands of families.

Around the state, Michiganders know him from his upstart 2018 campaign for
Governor. While he fell short in that race, voters didn’t hold that
against him. If anything, he got points for never wavering from his
platform over the past decade. He’s not just another politician — he’s
Abdul!

And perhaps more than anything else, he earned the trust of many voters by
being the only candidate to call Israel’s genocide in Gaza what it was,
even when it was politically inconvenient.

...WITH A TRUSTED MESSAGE:

MONEY OUT OF POLITICS, MONEY IN YOUR POCKET, MEDICARE FOR ALL

Clear, memorable, chantable. “Money out of Politics, Money in Your Pocket,
Medicare for All” quickly became shorthand for Abdul’s record and
platform, and the central rallying cry for our movement.

Whether they agreed with him on every issue, voters knew Abdul said what
he meant and meant what he said. His honesty, clarity and consistency
through changing political winds gave him a level of authenticity in
voters’ eyes that even $70 million couldn’t buy.

The level of trust and baseline respect Abdul has earned across the state
is intangible, yet will be invaluable in the general election —
particularly up against one of the most phony, corrupt, flip-flopping
politicians around: Mike Rogers.

THEY HAD MONEY, WE HAD PEOPLE
We didn’t have the money or the political establishment behind us, but we
had the people.

Our opponents had some of the biggest names in the Washington
establishment. We had the nurses, the teachers, and the almighty UAW.

Our opponents got endorsements of leaders at the top of Michigan’s
political food chain. We had the local leaders that know their communities
best: Wayne County Executive Warren Evans, Wayne County Commissioner
Martha G. Scott, Flint Mayor Sheldon Neeley and more.

A GOOD OLD FASHIONED CAMPAIGN (SORTA)
Especially early on, traditional media refused to take our campaign and
ideas seriously.

We knew the only way to overcome that establishment bias (and the $70
million we would ultimately face) would be to double down on in-person
organizing and online media — going everywhere and talking to everyone.

In the 474 days since launch, we held over 500 public events, including
townhalls, meet and greets, and rallies from Sault Ste. Marie to Ann
Arbor. Our dedicated team of 13,000 volunteers was able to collect nearly
30,000 signatures, knock over 200,000 doors, and make 1,000,000 calls. Our
greatest strength was, and remains, our people.

Online, our campaign continued our “go everywhere, talk to everyone”
approach. We grew an audience of hundreds of thousands, racking up
millions of impressions and tens of thousands of comments. We collaborated
with over 100 content creators from Michigan and around the country to
spread our message and continue to build grassroots momentum.

And we still showed up for traditional media. Abdul went on cable news
whenever they’d have him — even Fox News. We figured that when voters
heard from Abdul directly, they’d like him. We were right!

WHERE WE GO FROM HERE
We are grateful to Haley Stevens and Mallory McMorrow for running spirited
primary campaigns and for standing with us now to defeat Mike Rogers. We
welcome their voters into our movement with open arms — it’s going to take
all of us.

Over the next 13 weeks, we’re focused on winning over independent and
Republican voters around one vision: a Michigan that works for the working
many, not the powerful few.

This isn’t the race that Mike Rogers expected when he came out of his
retirement in Florida to launch his campaign 16 months ago. There’s no
Republican playbook to defeat a candidate like Abdul El-Sayed because they
have never faced a candidate like Abdul. He’s scrappy, strong, and has
never backed down from a fight.

It’s the race that we have been planning for 16 months.

Mike Rogers, we’re coming for you.

Peter,
Mike Rogers is better funded, better known, and better rested than we are
today. The only thing that closes that gap is grassroots support, which we
need a whole lot of now, not later.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260809-1-ak._EKcU5&amount=10&refcode=em20260809-2871&t=1006&akid=2882%2E251025%2EXIjVgD ]So please, chip in $10 or any amount so Abdul can start
Round 2 with the same fight he brought to Round 1.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260809-1-ak._EKcU5&amount=10&refcode=em20260809-2871&t=1025&akid=2882%2E251025%2EXIjVgD ]Donate $10 ››

Thanks so much,

Alia
Campaign Manager

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Emails like this help us stay connected with grassroots supporters like you, so thank you for taking the time to read this message. To contribute via check, please address it to Abdul for U.S. Senate, PO Box 126, St. Clair Shores, MI 48080.

Receive Fewer Emails: https://act.abdulformichigan.com/signup/receive-fewer-emails/?t=1026&akid=2882%2E251025%2EXIjVgD
Update Your Information: https://act.abdulformichigan.com/signup/update-your-information
Unsubscribe: https://act.abdulformichigan.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe?t=1027&akid=2882%2E251025%2EXIjVgD

Email us: info@abdulformichigan.com
Volunteer: https://go.abdulforsenate.com/

# [Healthcare For All Not Only Saves Money, but VISION!](https://bethfarnhamforcongress.com/2026/08/09/healthcare-for-all-not-only-saves-money-but-vision/?jetpack_skip_subscription_popup)
---
By **Elizabeth Farnham** on August 9, 2026
---
| **District Round-up 08.09.26**
---
Dear Neighbor, Thank you for reading my District Round-up. As your candidate for Pennsylvania’s 13th Congressional District, it is my honor and pleasure to deliver to you where I’ve been and what issues I’ve tackled in the past week. Criss-crossing the counties of Adams, Franklin, Fulton, Bedford, Cambria, Blair, Huntingdon, Mifflin, Juniata, Perry, Cumberland, and Somerset gives me great opportunities to meet with voters, hear what is on your hearts and minds, and the chance to voice my fight for Everyday Americans. If you would like to contribute to my campaign, please donate here:**[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/beth-farnham-for-congress-1](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=deec2d95ee03f1b584f89ba8f5475a0d6f4d0c184c4026f6249f9a562eb50635&blog_id=213069660&post_id=8531&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=7f59f390c06028026ee9b5eb2cf04263&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYWN0Ymx1ZS5jb20vZG9uYXRlL2JldGgtZmFybmhhbS1mb3ItY29uZ3Jlc3MtMQ=&email_id=453014dd41996ba9f8844918c71ca985)**
---
| **Healthcare for All!**
---
| |
---
When you can’t get the $750 injection directly into your eyeball, you will be sad.
---
Why?
---
Many thanks to Jane Palmer, Patient Advocacy & Clinical Outreach Manager Pennsylvania Retina Specialists, PC who helped to answer this question on a recent Thursday afternoon.
---
Because if you suffer retinopathy, a complication of diabetes, which is a pretty common disease in aging Americans, the solution is a monthly ($750-$3,740, actually) sight-saving injection into your eye, which your doctor feels is the best treatment, all in the comfort of your doctor’s office.
---
Unfortunately, the requirements to use less expensive drugs first, and go through the prior authorization process for Medicare Advantage is so complicated, that those paperwork delays can cost you time, resulting in more vision loss.
---
(Go ahead and take a gander at that flow chart, attached to this post.)
---
And more vision loss costs you the thing that more Americans have prized since before this country began.
---
Independence.
---
(In case you don’t know, losing independence in this country, especially in rural areas, is DEVASTATING.)
---
All because you were told you would save a little money choosing Medicare Advantage over regular Medicare.
---
Of course you may have chosen Medicare Advantage – it covers Medicare A needs, Medicare B, Dental needs, and Vision needs with no premium (except for Part B).
---
But the reason it’s cheaper for you is because Medicare Advantage has RULES.
---
And those rules MUST be followed.
---
So no, you can’t have the injection that will work best immediately for you.
---
You must go through their step process, trying drugs that don’t work, getting prior authorizations because you tried them, until you can finally have the medication that works.
---
However, during the months you were forced to try these subpar drugs, the disease progressed, and you lost even more vision.
---
If you were to skip the paperwork process and pay for the working medication on your own in order to keep your VISION, you would quickly be overwhelmed by the eternal cost of these injections.
---
The solution?
---
Healthcare for All.
---
Healthcare is a human right and every American citizen should be covered. If the United States were to grant healthcare to all of its citizens, the cost of healthcare would not only be thousands of dollars cheaper per capita, but we would live an average of four years longer.
---
Let’s stop the insanity of our patchwork healthcare system, including Medicare Advantage, so Americans can live long full lives and without medical debt.
---
If you want to check out what Healthcare for All might look like, take a look at Representative Jayapal’s Medicare for All bill in the comments. That is not necessarily a comprehensive plan, but it gives a national healthcare plan a starting point without reinventing the wheel.
---
And vote for me, Beth Farnham, on November 3rd, so that I can vote for Healthcare for All.
---
Together, we #ChooseDemocracy and Good Health!
---
| |
---
| **Relating to Conservative Voters**
---
| |
---
In the deepest, reddest county in Pennsylvania, the gentleman asked me, “So, how does a politician like you get involved?”
---
Many thanks to the Fulton County Democratic Committee for hosting a tent at the Fulton County Fair on Thursday evening. I spoke to voters from all corners of the district, even when they said they wouldn’t vote for me.
---
I answered him as I knew best – by the timeline I had lived.
---
In August of 2015, I, as a lifelong Republican, had a baby. Yet six months later, amid diaper changes, nursing, and a fitful sleep schedule, Trump, a known grifter who had cheated those who worked for him and cheated multiple spouses, had landed on my radar. He was winning primary elections...and so was Clinton.
---
“You know,” I said to my (also Republican) husband in February of 2016, “If it ever comes down to an election between Trump and Clinton, I think I’m voting for Clinton.”
---
“Really?” he asked.
---
“Yeah,” I responded.
---
So I told the man that Rob and I had voted for different Republicans in the primary election of 2016 but obviously Trump had won.
---
We looked at Clinton’s voting record in Congress. Remembering her experience as a First Lady, her education as a lawyer, and her service as former Secretary of State, we were impressed by her experience, education, and competence.
---
Then, we did the work, engaging friends, family, church members, and every Republican we knew, asking them not to vote for Trump and any Republican who supported him because he was a threat to our national security on a variety of levels.
---
It didn’t matter. I had voted straight Democrat because every other local Republican stood with Trump, but they voted for Trump and he won. I was in grief for our country. After a healing visit with family, I was ready to DO SOMETHING. I couldn’t stop Trump from swearing in, but I could join the first protest of his presidency. And so I joined the Women’s March in January 2017. Penn Live even captured me holding my pocket Constitution aloft.
---
After that demonstration, I joined others, and grassroots groups, and I kept voting Democrat, even in the primaries when I had to write in Democratic names on my Republican ballots. After so many votes, I told Rob, “I think I’m a Democrat. I’m going to change my registration.” I did, and a few months later, he did the same.
---
Years later, I joined the Democratic Committee. When I discovered in 2022 that we didn’t have a Democratic candidate to oppose our election-denier of a US Representative, multimillionaire John Joyce, I ran a write-in campaign. It wasn’t something I had to think about for too long – I love my country.
---
The gentleman listened to my story, politely nodding, but I felt like I was missing something.
---
I asked what mattered to him about candidates and he mentioned it was important to learn about our views because he wanted to know if they aligned with his. I pointed out my website on my brochure.
---
Still, I couldn’t shake the feeling I needed to connect better. I took a chance and stated, “You know John Joyce isn’t just an election denier, he voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act that raises Affordable Care Act premiums.”
---
That was it, I had hit the nail on the head. He lifted his eyes to mine then lowered them, stating that his had gone up. I offered that many had gone up hundreds of dollars per person. His partner, who had been standing quietly by his side, chimed in, “Ours went up 4 times as much. We can’t afford it, so we don’t have health insurance now.”
---
This, this is the devastation that John Joyce, a dermatologist no less, brings to our 13th Congressional District. John Joyce doesn’t care about the people left in his wake of dangerous votes. He only wants Trump’s favor.
---
But it doesn’t have to be this way.
---
I asked the gentleman and his significant other to please vote for me. They went away, pretty much nodding, but still keen to review my website which is just fine with me.
---
Please vote for me, Beth Farnham, on November 3rd.
---
When you do, you not only #ChooseDemocracy, you choose our local community.
---

| | **Measles on the Rise in Pennsylvania!**
---
| |
---
Measles cases continue to climb in Pennsylvania. In PA-13, the counties of Bedford, Mifflin, and Perry have been affected.
---
Measles is a highly contagious disease that truly sickens, and even maims or kills children. Sometimes, very young children who recover, suffer years later, the fatal complication of subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) and die.
---
Measles also wipes out immunity from years prior, rendering children more vulnerable to diseases they had previously been vaccinated against like polio and chicken pox.
---
Please have your children vaccinated by the schedule approved by the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP).
---
If you’re a Gen-Xer who only received one measles shot like me, please have your doctor test your titer to see if you need a booster.
---
And please check with other parents about their vaccine philosophy so you can decide about how much you expose your children to those of parents who don’t believe in evidence-based science.
---
Even the antivaxxer RFK Jr is starting to come around, though it was his anti vaccine rhetoric that contributed to this preventable crisis in the first place.
---
Together, we #ChooseDemocracy and the good health of our community!
---
