As your candidate for Pennsylvania’s 13th Congressional District, it is my honor and pleasure to deliver to you where I’ve been and what issues I’ve tackled in the past week. Criss-crossing the counties of Adams, Franklin, Fulton, Bedford, Cambria, Blair, Huntingdon, Mifflin, Juniata, Perry, Cumberland, and Somerset gives me great opportunities to meet with voters, hear what is on your hearts and minds, and the chance to voice my fight for Everyday Americans. If you would like to contribute to my campaign, please donate here: | Healthcare for All! | | When you can’t get the $750 injection directly into your eyeball, you will be sad. Why? Many thanks to Jane Palmer, Patient Advocacy & Clinical Outreach Manager Pennsylvania Retina Specialists, PC who helped to answer this question on a recent Thursday afternoon. Because if you suffer retinopathy, a complication of diabetes, which is a pretty common disease in aging Americans, the solution is a monthly ($750-$3,740, actually) sight-saving injection into your eye, which your doctor feels is the best treatment, all in the comfort of your doctor’s office. Unfortunately, the requirements to use less expensive drugs first, and go through the prior authorization process for Medicare Advantage is so complicated, that those paperwork delays can cost you time, resulting in more vision loss. (Go ahead and take a gander at that flow chart, attached to this post.) And more vision loss costs you the thing that more Americans have prized since before this country began. Independence. (In case you don’t know, losing independence in this country, especially in rural areas, is DEVASTATING.) All because you were told you would save a little money choosing Medicare Advantage over regular Medicare. Of course you may have chosen Medicare Advantage – it covers Medicare A needs, Medicare B, Dental needs, and Vision needs with no premium (except for Part B). But the reason it’s cheaper for you is because Medicare Advantage has RULES. And those rules MUST be followed. So no, you can’t have the injection that will work best immediately for you. You must go through their step process, trying drugs that don’t work, getting prior authorizations because you tried them, until you can finally have the medication that works. However, during the months you were forced to try these subpar drugs, the disease progressed, and you lost even more vision. If you were to skip the paperwork process and pay for the working medication on your own in order to keep your VISION, you would quickly be overwhelmed by the eternal cost of these injections. The solution? Healthcare for All. Healthcare is a human right and every American citizen should be covered. If the United States were to grant healthcare to all of its citizens, the cost of healthcare would not only be thousands of dollars cheaper per capita, but we would live an average of four years longer. Let’s stop the insanity of our patchwork healthcare system, including Medicare Advantage, so Americans can live long full lives and without medical debt. If you want to check out what Healthcare for All might look like, take a look at Representative Jayapal’s Medicare for All bill in the comments. That is not necessarily a comprehensive plan, but it gives a national healthcare plan a starting point without reinventing the wheel. And vote for me, Beth Farnham, on November 3rd, so that I can vote for Healthcare for All. Together, we #ChooseDemocracy and Good Health! | | | Relating to Conservative Voters | | In the deepest, reddest county in Pennsylvania, the gentleman asked me, “So, how does a politician like you get involved?” Many thanks to the Fulton County Democratic Committee for hosting a tent at the Fulton County Fair on Thursday evening. I spoke to voters from all corners of the district, even when they said they wouldn’t vote for me. I answered him as I knew best – by the timeline I had lived. In August of 2015, I, as a lifelong Republican, had a baby. Yet six months later, amid diaper changes, nursing, and a fitful sleep schedule, Trump, a known grifter who had cheated those who worked for him and cheated multiple spouses, had landed on my radar. He was winning primary elections...and so was Clinton. “You know,” I said to my (also Republican) husband in February of 2016, “If it ever comes down to an election between Trump and Clinton, I think I’m voting for Clinton.” “Really?” he asked. “Yeah,” I responded. So I told the man that Rob and I had voted for different Republicans in the primary election of 2016 but obviously Trump had won. We looked at Clinton’s voting record in Congress. Remembering her experience as a First Lady, her education as a lawyer, and her service as former Secretary of State, we were impressed by her experience, education, and competence. Then, we did the work, engaging friends, family, church members, and every Republican we knew, asking them not to vote for Trump and any Republican who supported him because he was a threat to our national security on a variety of levels. It didn’t matter. I had voted straight Democrat because every other local Republican stood with Trump, but they voted for Trump and he won. I was in grief for our country. After a healing visit with family, I was ready to DO SOMETHING. I couldn’t stop Trump from swearing in, but I could join the first protest of his presidency. And so I joined the Women’s March in January 2017. Penn Live even captured me holding my pocket Constitution aloft. After that demonstration, I joined others, and grassroots groups, and I kept voting Democrat, even in the primaries when I had to write in Democratic names on my Republican ballots. After so many votes, I told Rob, “I think I’m a Democrat. I’m going to change my registration.” I did, and a few months later, he did the same. Years later, I joined the Democratic Committee. When I discovered in 2022 that we didn’t have a Democratic candidate to oppose our election-denier of a US Representative, multimillionaire John Joyce, I ran a write-in campaign. It wasn’t something I had to think about for too long – I love my country. The gentleman listened to my story, politely nodding, but I felt like I was missing something. I asked what mattered to him about candidates and he mentioned it was important to learn about our views because he wanted to know if they aligned with his. I pointed out my website on my brochure. Still, I couldn’t shake the feeling I needed to connect better. I took a chance and stated, “You know John Joyce isn’t just an election denier, he voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act that raises Affordable Care Act premiums.” That was it, I had hit the nail on the head. He lifted his eyes to mine then lowered them, stating that his had gone up. I offered that many had gone up hundreds of dollars per person. His partner, who had been standing quietly by his side, chimed in, “Ours went up 4 times as much. We can’t afford it, so we don’t have health insurance now.” This, this is the devastation that John Joyce, a dermatologist no less, brings to our 13th Congressional District. John Joyce doesn’t care about the people left in his wake of dangerous votes. He only wants Trump’s favor. But it doesn’t have to be this way. I asked the gentleman and his significant other to please vote for me. They went away, pretty much nodding, but still keen to review my website which is just fine with me. Please vote for me, Beth Farnham, on November 3rd. When you do, you not only #ChooseDemocracy, you choose our local community. | | Dear Friend,

How much do you know about the Electoral College?

It's an important topic, and one vital to our nation's future.

You see, a movement is growing, led by progressives but supported by many well-meaning Americans, to change the way we elect our president.

**Their goal: to get rid of the Electoral College altogether, and "move beyond" the Constitution and Declaration. **

**That 's why I hope you'll take our National Quiz on Presidential Selection today.** It's a quick and engaging way to test your own understanding of how our presidents are elected.

**You can take your quiz by using the secure link below:**

[https://info.hillsdale.edu/hillsdale-college-national-quiz-on-presidential-selection](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/s/c/GrA-2Rt4-VDMHe7G_SW3UIrN-QH0ADHlgLRv_2Na2QGxZoHm-vvuwE34eN_Awkdvnf146w_OIcHyiI9z_uYwp35a8lisaLGh5VVF2F95zKmO_B9eQTUm9PwgCW_qYD6Q6g-AaIVwPbiZeV2lKODkVGSxIM5RFW1FRsJ4JPoYCkfxPQrn1smLYXi-cDiZEc0ElymXRyXQc3-1lgV-0MHCyuVp3SQ1T1QtmgI6gIaCef1a7xalTq_EM1wVvezjBoZRj0ENNOgqjRzRK029Z5pqfcoUZSQDf_N-5AsUET5QEAVKFz-80oO3SagV2TgGzQHXIWAmNS2TbF99oBjxH2qolLJr166Ltvjslrh0_wg_qO8JBtZbeEanjtelBeD1Z9B4dQ83vfxLRR-xxmkKbZYU33i9W4UUN7TkdIn0ZGewiuHXy94GKHZivq8J1hY4qI6oEqL2xdGooFMqpqsyNveCON74LlCSnc0mpOfqgyXTehR-M40feM8GQcybe58zrcZRAOvW1iTDeu_hSz7sJg3S2jm0k6totHLLr75CUivp_p5BbapFHVKjw_JzvnELIl_1EAt1FbsEAYSfEMBkOJkkVUR-BvVoGiVUHWnsKl6cKWPl7rkIo8mTeoOYCHXQ32WlxJQprWegQZ8_h_ikZddR1cac7GfXiJ2qQfkgqMx0kws0AFG1i2J0NVL8d2s7XaVNlwcK9vekDcYL5bqGyelqGRiRJuZd69MOu7uHWXhbivX3pVonRG7Wirr77XwMeLiL_tgEk9KOn_5jI8ES7eEab6Xddn0haZwq6tn2d224n8k_zPmo5srFsisU73b7rlHtrw/h0k-phl-GKJNQdnB_d43qH9gfzBmw9Tt/23)

For most of our history, the Electoral College was uncontroversial. It was understood to be a safeguard for free and representative government.

**But today, dozens of states have joined together to undermine this key constitutional protection.**

The push to "move beyond" the Constitution stems from the failure of too many schools to teach American civics properly. Many citizens today don't fully understand the importance of the Constitution and the Electoral College in preserving liberty.

To counter this, Hillsdale College has expanded its educational mission on behalf of liberty nationwide, **reaching and teaching millions** of Americans in all 50 states.

When you take the **National Quiz on Presidential Selection** , you'll gain a clearer understanding of how the Electoral College upholds liberty--and you'll have the opportunity to **share this** information with your fellow Americans.

So please take your **National Quiz on Presidential Selection**. It will only take a few minutes of your time.

**You can take the quiz using the secure link I 've provided below: **

[https://info.hillsdale.edu/hillsdale-college-national-quiz-on-presidential-selection](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/s/c/vR954H9UYJ0ePZM_qa0K8G9XFD1wJ0b0BXu18w_9wUcFLI2dDsLO801Mj9ZwQklp7lgAzY3n572EaH6GC3RbkmcxX-ixcb3eYpLuUYlvzGHGCz8uaFeiwBdPf2h18F0wj49u7wwjSAMisLO-aY53k0MjxQEW74zpKNo0TIsws0Uq6q-jbTaMBLyhf9p4J6U0GESX18nU2bjfTjUjSvLDKE2jB2-dpJuwnKb0jDUS48uD_DEx55UeFZmjDFKCS_4QH7ssP33Zx3mFSheDhzn899QNV1lomryn_eBBs3gZ95s9zXLkwpCdVGW0aLqs5pNhPHdFf4WZBuz4k81xN8Oh_LCndq1MiaBpdGav3m76vCi4ISKN_-B3ngJl6An7nsVhRcQAXtS6y4KLM5aQ8z1sBLHXnrNoIXXKjJSsUkpv3AZEy7ZzUvH4Y5Wvv9R_sW_lpcMMts4ko6KTxnywyK0ZZC5TQ1A3SSceq1ck1YqwAcfnNBA2O_svklXnqmDEa6cue6UJw6I2pWuFp8z0cUAZXcY-qVJMsU7pcrff7N6nIKbAc5im-5gwYqORBoLEBoLBAdswTxXgTNJ61lRxBG700xUnk6b6-T1joS2lrWkti1GCJh5Oo-Ir3nYvcXhjADP8_4tDedMjXagGy2PXFXp_BJuJFKi-cwvyzmitQv-xc4qEsUK0-5B8uQivi7VeocOmfJxRrxZJTE6JqjqijHmRet4jDpsdPQ3Bl3TavOuyUFE_Z53T1w9M7r0OcWwLgUJ6g46NjrtYkHg1osGuc6RanHov-P09l4al-t3-ogDWtwQ2FXLbYFREXBsZyTLuCVotPQ/i-VISG7_VR2gD1Ue2hdCO2MLomWuZfBZ/23)

**As a thank-you for taking the quiz, I 'll send you a free 12-minute video with a Hillsdale College professor that explains the history and purpose of the Electoral College. **

The video provides a concise, engaging, and insightful overview of the Electoral College and its significance. It would be a great resource to send to a friend or a family member!

One other thing.

Hillsdale refuses EVERY PENNY of government funding--even indirectly through student loans or grants--so that we can pursue truth and defend liberty independent of meddling bureaucrats in Washington, D.C. That's why your support matters so much.

So, after you take your quiz, please also consider giving a **tax-deductible gift of $35, $50, or even $100** to help us share this video with millions of Americans--especially young people who don't understand how the Constitution preserves liberty through the Electoral College. Your gift also funds our other nationwide educational outreach.

Fellow Patriot - I'm not a politician. In fact, I've never run for office before.

I never expected to be running for office. I have never had any desire to be a politician. I am doing this because I am answering President Donald Trump's call to serve and want to stand up for South Carolina and fight for his agenda.

_**Like Lindsey, I am a hard worker with a servant's heart.**_ We grew up in the back of a bar and liquor store, in one room. Our parents worked hard every day to make ends meet - there was no time for sickness and few vacations, because if the doors weren't open, no money was coming in.

What I've spent my life doing is serving South Carolina - including running a state agency with 130 employees and a $90 million budget. We have a decision to make.

_**“Crossroads.” “A defining moment.” “Turning point.”**_ Whatever you call it, this election is going to test whether Pennsylvania keeps choosing leaders who solve problems — or we let Donald Trump’s allies drag our Commonwealth backward. **I know which side I’m on, Derek.** I’m fighting for a Pennsylvania where kids can get a good education, families can afford a good life, workers are treated with dignity, and every person has the freedom to build their own future. And that’s what we’ve been focused on from day one: Reopening I-95 in 12 days, delivering free school breakfast, cutting taxes ten times, investing in safer communities, and getting stuff done. But Derek, none of that progress is guaranteed. My far-right opponent has Donald Trump and National Republicans in her corner. They know Pennsylvania is the most important battleground state in the country. And they know that if they flip this Governor’s office, the far-right will control every state-level office in our Commonwealth. That’s not a risk we can afford to take, Derek. On August 4th, the "Show Me State" **[overwhelmingly rejected](https://substack.com/redirect/c2ba7da4-5969-48bb-a796-d4283666e0ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** a referendum to phase-out state income tax, a devastating 84-17 split which tells me that casual socialism and confiscatory practices masquerading as duty to "the poor" have gripped even the reddest of states.
This does not bode well for the future of America.
One of the leading voices urging voters to oppose this measure was **[The Catholic Hierarchy](https://substack.com/redirect/9deceb1b-4111-4aaa-b22f-f0b98f3fb80c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ,** and this disappoints me gravely. I love my Catholic faith, but I wish my Catholic Church were not so... stupid. It often is. I thought Pope Marxis had died... but I guess his spirit of Liberation Theology which rejects the free market and celebrates the state will live on for quite some time.
But, let me tackle one thing at a time. First let me render to Ceasar, then to Church.

As for Caesar, let us now rename Missouri the "Take Mine" state, and that is what income tax does. We should categorically reject the notion that the state may confiscate from our productivity, let alone third parties be entitled to redistribution from the same. Our founders saw this so clearly, knew that taxing income was so pernicious as well as endless, that they forbade income tax in the U.S. Constitution at the federal level.
Lucky for us, progressives 113 years ago won the votes for the 16th Amendment, modifying the sacred text so that Washington could take from your paycheck. Fret not, for the congressman who authored the nation's first income tax bill, democrat Cordell Hull, **[assured us](https://substack.com/redirect/7dd7994f-f4b3-4bfb-87d5-847dc97e3557?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** the income tax would ONLY target the "very rich" and it would ONLY be around 1%.
Surprise, surprise, a democrat lied.
Not only did the federal income tax (along with its bastard sibling the 17th Amendment) implode the concept of Federalism, weaken the states, and spawn the demon called "the federal government" but it altered a once healthy understanding of property rights. Now, the government skims from your earnings. Just 1%. Ok, 7%. 15%. Let's just make it a cool 26% unless you're "rich" and then we go to 30% or 37%.
BUT NO MORE!

* * *
* * *
Unless you are Elon Musk. Then, a new proposed tax, a "billionaire's tax" and to justify the endless appetite of government income tax whores, they bring out to the cameras a fat slob who somehow, for some ungodly reason, got pregnant nine times but claims to be "disabled" and wants a new cell phone. For you see, the poor are because of the rich, and not because of personal choices, and only government taking your wealth fix it.
This was the undercurrent of President Lyndon Johnson's "Great Society" program. Government programs and government workers, well-funded through by taxing "the rich" will eliminate poverty in America. Since then, we have spent an **[estimated $22 trillion](https://substack.com/redirect/8842200a-11e7-4a16-a78d-fd1dda45180b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on programs to help "the poor" and all we have to show for it is the same level of poverty along with endless "nonprofits" taking tax dollars to help with and paying their executives handsomely.
Charities focused on "the poor" are often run by bored housewives with lavish salaries all paid by our confiscated funds. Example: Governor Gavin Newsom's own wife, Jennifer Siebel, the "First Partner" (lame) of California **[makes hundreds of thousands](https://substack.com/redirect/20f34d9e-fc65-4fea-883b-4b469b2b7322?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** of dollars in non-profits that care about "the poor" and "the children". Californians must be thrilled knowing their tax dollars go to such "causes".
This was the "what about the poor" fear-mongering which crushed Missouri's referendum. The local Bishops said "those with greater resources bear a proportionately greater share of the public burden" while the head of Missouri Catholic Charities **[told voters](https://substack.com/redirect/9deceb1b-4111-4aaa-b22f-f0b98f3fb80c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to "remember the poor first and foremost". What utter nonsense. This idea that the poor in America are some perpetual victims of unjust structures and not their own decision making is offensive.
Show me a mother at a food pantry who doesn't have a $800 tattoo of her children on her breasts. The buses of "poor" arriving at Atlantic City Casinos are full of able-bodied people gambling with EBT cards. I've seen "poor" people buy Kerry Gold Butter at $6.99 per lb. with food stamps while I buy Giant's own brand on sale. And I have a job.
One Christmas some 20 years ago, friends asked me to volunteer at The Mission on 14th Street NW in Washington, DC to distribute toys for the needy, and full of Christmas Cheer I agreed. About 30 minutes into my shift, I helped a woman bring free toys to her car: a double-parked Lexus SUV.
I left. "The Poor". Give me a break.
* * *
* * *
## The Capitalist is a reader-supported publication, we exist for you, because of you!
[Support What We Do](https://substack.com/redirect/57fc6783-c0d6-4c56-aa69-e960700d1fc7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
That is my experience of "the poor" in America. Yes, there are poor people who are truly needy and royally f'd, and they need assistance, and I would be in so much a better position to help them if I had more money. I don't because government has taken half, and once again we shall quote our Lord "The poor you will always have with you". It's like He knew something we didn't.
So long as we have this belief that person A has, but person B does not have, so person C can take and give, we have a major flaw in our thinking. Not just our economic thinking, but sociological, cultural, and even moral. It is quite literally "robbing Peter to pay Paul" and yet the Church has succumbed to it. Tragic.
Of course, I am not an anarchist. I understand we need some government, and that very limited government needs funding. So, when Missouri proponents of the income tax repeal stipulated that the revenue shortfall would come from increase sales tax, I celebrated it.
Why? Because I am cheap.
I don't have a new phone. In fact, I broke it recently and need a new screen, but it still works fine. My TVs are old but work fine. My truck is a 2018, my better half's jeep is a 2017. Most of my clothes are from Costco. I have three pairs of nice shoes that are almost 15 years old, which I polish myself and get soled when needed by a local cobbler (yes, they are still around). I don't go to movies. I prefer to cook at home, and groceries are exempt from sales tax.
So, you tell me, which system should I prefer? The one stipulated on the aforementioned poor who, in all likelihood, get weekly manicures and a daily 4000 calorie, venti, white chocolate mocha hazelnut caramel frappa-diabetes with extra whipped cream paying MORE taxes on her purchases, or me, parsimonious, abstemious, me, keeping all of my own earnings?
It isn't really a hard choice, is it? It does not make me greedy, for no one is greedier than the government official, or, sadly, the Missouri Catholic Bishop, who thinks he is entitled to my labor. Why am I greedy and selfish wanting to keep what I earned?
The Church has thoroughly disappointed me yet again. Our faith leaders should ENCOURAGE work and DISCOURAGE spending. They should welcome more earning and frown upon more consumerism. Of course, you are going to need a couch or a fridge or a car, and the higher taxes are going to stink. Of course. But maybe, just maybe, your current items aren't all that bad, and keeping up with the Joneses should have a cost.
Missourians have disappointed me, too. Not just the intellectual failure recognizing many states do not have an income and have lower poverty rates, but the moral failure thinking the government has a right to earnings and will somehow solve poverty with it. Socialism, disguised as Christian Charity, creeping into government, our culture, our churches, and our tax code. I will abide by it, but I will not succumb to it or keep silent on it.
**Honor and courage.**

And you can still get in at $0.52/share before August 14.. Disclosures Potential Uber return for Marc Cuban does not take into account dilution. The Deloitte rankings are based on submitted applications and public company database research, with winners selected based on their fiscal-year revenue growth percentage over a three-year period in 2023. Please read the offering circular at invest.modemobile.com. This is a paid advertisement for Mode Mobile 's Regulation A Offering. As for Caesar, let us now rename Missouri the "Take Mine" state, and that is what income tax does. We should categorically reject the notion that the state may confiscate from our productivity, let alone third parties be entitled to redistribution from the same. Our founders saw this so clearly, knew that taxing income was so pernicious as well as endless, that they forbade income tax in the U.S. Constitution at the federal level. Lucky for us, progressives 113 years ago won the votes for the 16th Amendment, modifying the sacred text so that Washington could take from your paycheck. Fret not, for the congressman who authored the nation's first income tax bill, democrat Cordell Hull, the income tax would ONLY target the "very rich" and it would ONLY be around 1%. Surprise, surprise, a democrat lied. Not only did the federal income tax (along with its bastard sibling the 17th Amendment) implode the concept of Federalism, weaken the states, and spawn the demon called "the federal government" but it altered a once healthy understanding of property rights. Now, the government skims from your earnings. Just 1%. Ok, 7%. 15%. Let's just make it a cool 26% unless you're "rich" and then we go to 30% or 37%. BUT NO MORE! | | | | ---|---|--- | Jul 14 | Unless you are Elon Musk. Then, a new proposed tax, a "billionaire's tax" and to justify the endless appetite of government income tax whores, they bring out to the cameras a fat slob who somehow, for some ungodly reason, got pregnant nine times but claims to be "disabled" and wants a new cell phone. For you see, the poor are because of the rich, and not because of personal choices, and only government taking your wealth fix it. This was the undercurrent of President Lyndon Johnson's "Great Society" program. Government programs and government workers, well-funded through by taxing "the rich" will eliminate poverty in America. Since then, we have spent an on programs to help "the poor" and all we have to show for it is the same level of poverty along with endless "nonprofits" taking tax dollars to help with and paying their executives handsomely. Charities focused on "the poor" are often run by bored housewives with lavish salaries all paid by our confiscated funds. Example: Governor Gavin Newsom's own wife, Jennifer Siebel, the "First Partner" (lame) of California of dollars in non-profits that care about "the poor" and "the children". Californians must be thrilled knowing their tax dollars go to such "causes". This was the "what about the poor" fear-mongering which crushed Missouri's referendum. The local Bishops said "those with greater resources bear a proportionately greater share of the public burden" while the head of Missouri Catholic Charities to "remember the poor first and foremost". What utter nonsense. This idea that the poor in America are some perpetual victims of unjust structures and not their own decision making is offensive. Show me a mother at a food pantry who doesn't have a $800 tattoo of her children on her breasts. The buses of "poor" arriving at Atlantic City Casinos are full of able-bodied people gambling with EBT cards. I've seen "poor" people buy Kerry Gold Butter at $6.99 per lb. with food stamps while I buy Giant's own brand on sale. And I have a job. One Christmas some 20 years ago, friends asked me to volunteer at The Mission on 14th Street NW in Washington, DC to distribute toys for the needy, and full of Christmas Cheer I agreed. About 30 minutes into my shift, I helped a woman bring free toys to her car: a double-parked Lexus SUV. I left. "The Poor". Give me a break. The Capitalist is a reader-supported publication, we exist for you, because of you! That is my experience of "the poor" in America. Yes, there are poor people who are truly needy and royally f'd, and they need assistance, and I would be in so much a better position to help them if I had more money. I don't because government has taken half, and once again we shall quote our Lord "The poor you will always have with you". It's like He knew something we didn't. So long as we have this belief that person A has, but person B does not have, so person C can take and give, we have a major flaw in our thinking. Not just our economic thinking, but sociological, cultural, and even moral. It is quite literally "robbing Peter to pay Paul" and yet the Church has succumbed to it. Tragic. Of course, I am not an anarchist. I understand we need some government, and that very limited government needs funding. So, when Missouri proponents of the income tax repeal stipulated that the revenue shortfall would come from increase sales tax, I celebrated it. Why? Because I am cheap. I don't have a new phone. In fact, I broke it recently and need a new screen, but it still works fine. My TVs are old but work fine. My truck is a 2018, my better half's jeep is a 2017. Most of my clothes are from Costco. I have three pairs of nice shoes that are almost 15 years old, which I polish myself and get soled when needed by a local cobbler (yes, they are still around). I don't go to movies. I prefer to cook at home, and groceries are exempt from sales tax. So, you tell me, which system should I prefer? The one stipulated on the aforementioned poor who, in all likelihood, get weekly manicures and a daily 4000 calorie, venti, white chocolate mocha hazelnut caramel frappa-diabetes with extra whipped cream paying MORE taxes on her purchases, or me, parsimonious, abstemious, me, keeping all of my own earnings? It isn't really a hard choice, is it? It does not make me greedy, for no one is greedier than the government official, or, sadly, the Missouri Catholic Bishop, who thinks he is entitled to my labor. Why am I greedy and selfish wanting to keep what I earned? The Church has thoroughly disappointed me yet again. Our faith leaders should ENCOURAGE work and DISCOURAGE spending. They should welcome more earning and frown upon more consumerism. Of course, you are going to need a couch or a fridge or a car, and the higher taxes are going to stink. Of course. But maybe, just maybe, your current items aren't all that bad, and keeping up with the Joneses should have a cost. Missourians have disappointed me, too. Not just the intellectual failure recognizing many states do not have an income and have lower poverty rates, but the moral failure thinking the government has a right to earnings and will somehow solve poverty with it. Socialism, disguised as Christian Charity, creeping into government, our culture, our churches, and our tax code. I will abide by it, but I will not succumb to it or keep silent on it. Honor and courage. Daniel Turner is the founder and executive director of Power The Future, a national nonprofit organization that advocates for American energy jobs. During COVID, the public schools were shut down across Ohio – forced into isolation, screens, and chaos.
Chronic absenteeism exploded. Learning gaps widened. Mental health crises surged. Kids in working-class families fell further behind, while some private schools stayed open and did just fine.
And the person responsible for leading that shutdown? My radical opponent, Democrat Amy Acton.
---
[](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)
---
While families begged for normalcy, she doubled down on mandates, closures, and fear. And now, she wants a promotion – from the architect of school closures to the Governor’s Mansion.

Not on my watch.

Ohio’s students deserve an apology. But let’s be honest: we won’t get one. The Left never admits when they’re wrong – they just double down.

**That’s why I’m stepping up. I’m running for Governor to empower parents, protect kids, and make sure Ohio NEVER shuts down its classrooms again.**

But I can’t win this fight alone. We need to get our message out – on TV, online, everywhere – and that takes serious resources.

**[So, I’m humbly asking: Will you chip in just a few bucks to my campaign today?](https://trk.email.vivekforohio._x_LMMs5U2g)**

The media will protect Amy Acton and her failed lockdown legacy. The Democrats will fund her.

But the people of Ohio remember what happened – and we won’t let it happen again.

**Vivek Ramaswamy**

Donald Trump has been sued
more than 750 times since he took office.

750 times.

And in more than 450 of those cases, judges have let Trump's policies stay
in effect — while the lawsuits are still being fought.^1

For years, Trump and his allies have stacked the courts — from district
benches all the way to the Supreme Court — with loyalist judges who'd
rubber-stamp whatever he wanted, whenever he wanted it.

And look at just some of the chaos it’s allowed to ensue:

* Trump attempted to end birthright citizenship
* He froze federal funding to entire states
* He tried to fire a sitting Federal Reserve governor over accusations
she was never even charged with
* He fired the watchdogs whose job is to hold him accountable
* He punished a law firm for refusing to do free legal work for his
agenda
* He's using a wartime law from the 1700s to deport people without due
process.

This is the system Trump built: push unconstitutional, self-serving
policies. Get sued. Fall back on the cronies he installed on the bench to
keep it running long enough to do the damage. Cash in while the courts
slow-walk justice.

Demand Justice PAC exists to fight exactly this — to expose judicial
corruption and Trump’s court takeover scheme, and demand accountability
from the courts Trump has his grip on.

If the _“SAVE America” Act_ became law, it would require everyone to present a passport, or a birth certificate with their current name, in order to register to vote or update their voter registration. But:
* Many Natives and other people of color lack birth certificates.

* 70 million women have changed their names, and so have many trans Americans.

* 150 million Americans don’t have a passport. Many can’t afford their basic needs right now, so they certainly can’t afford the cost of getting photos taken, the $165 passport processing fee, and shipping.

**Republicans want to implement a modern-day poll tax, disproportionately harming women, naturalized citizens, seniors, and Black, brown, trans, and working class people.**
Trump, Republicans in Congress, and the billionaire oligarchs influencing them are scared of our collective power. That’s why they’re trying to suppress our votes.
In these last few months before November’s midterm elections, we must come together to defend our voting rights from increased attacks.

Thank you for taking action.
This week, Trump spread lies about “election fraud” in Wayne County, which includes part of my congressional district. He’s targeting majority-Black Detroit because he wants to weaken our progressive power.
He’s done this before, as part of his attempts to suppress our votes. But we will keep standing up to Trump and fighting for our voting rights, especially as we head toward this November’s general election.
**I promise to continue fighting for Americans’ needs and rights in Congress.**
Although the _Voting Rights Act_ has largely been dismantled, we still have the constitutional rights that it was created to enforce. Congress must urgently restore and expand the _Voting Rights Act_ ’s protections by passing new laws.
I’m co-sponsoring many policies to defend and expand our right to vote, such as the _Fair Representation Act_ , the _John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act_ , the _Expanding the VOTE Act_ , the _Universal Right To Vote by Mail Act_ , the _Vote at Home Act_ , the _Time Off to Vote Act_ , and the _Youth Voting Rights Act_.
Despite the backlash against our progress and attacks on our constitutional rights, our movement is strong and growing larger. And more broadly, the American people are overwhelmingly aligned on many progressive issues. For example, most voters support Medicare for All.
Together, we’re pushing our government toward the promise of American democracy — a government of, by, and for the people, where our representatives actually represent us and fight for our needs.
With you in the fight for better,
Rashida

clean_body: They’re trying to suppress our votes because they’re scared of our power. | | | Friend, This week, Trump spread lies about “election fraud” in Wayne County, which includes part of my congressional district and majority-Black Detroit. He’s targeted us before because he wants to weaken our progressive power. And with this November’s general election approaching, Trump and Republicans in Congress are increasing their attacks on our voting rights. The Fascist-In-Chief is trying to restrict our access to mail-in voting. His followers in the House of Representatives recently passed parts of the “SAVE America” Act — a voter suppression bill that could disenfranchise more than 100 million Americans — in a budget bill that’s now in the Senate. We must push back. ****** | Thank you for taking action. I promise to keep fighting for you and your rights in Congress. Please check out yesterday’s email or the above petition page to learn more about the “SAVE America” Act and the policies I’m co-sponsoring to protect and expand our voting rights. Always serving you, Rashida \---------- Forwarded message --------- From: Rashida Tlaib**** Date: Sat, Aug 8, 2026 Subject: Sign to demand Congress reject voter suppression bills and pass policies to expand our voting rights To: dpwillis67@gmail.com Friend, This year, Trump’s nominees to the Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act , prompting a slew of southern states to disenfranchise and weaken the power of Black voters. But progressive Tennessee state legislator Justin Pearson just won his primary election anyway , even though he had to pivot last-minute and campaign in a newly redrawn, no-longer-majority-Black district! If he wins against a Republican in November, Justin will join me in the House of Representatives. Together we’ll fight for your rights and make Congress act as a check on the President. Right now, the Fascist-In-Chief is trying to attack our access to mail-in ballots before this November’s midterm elections, which could shift control of the House and Senate. And Republicans in the House of Representatives recently pushed through parts of the Trump-backed “SAVE America” Act , which would block millions of eligible Americans from registering to vote or updating their voter registration. That’s part of a budget bill that’s now in the Senate. The Senate has rejected the SAVE Act before, and must do so again. **** If the “SAVE America” Act became law, it would require everyone to present a passport, or a birth certificate with their current name, in order to register to vote or update their voter registration. But: Many Natives and other people of color lack birth certificates. 70 million women have changed their names, and so have many trans Americans. 150 million Americans don’t have a passport. Many can’t afford their basic needs right now, so they certainly can’t afford the cost of getting photos taken, the $165 passport processing fee, and shipping. Republicans want to implement a modern-day poll tax, disproportionately harming women, naturalized citizens, seniors, and Black, brown, trans, and working class people. Trump, Republicans in Congress, and the billionaire oligarchs influencing them are scared of our collective power. That’s why they’re trying to suppress our votes. In these last few months before November’s midterm elections, we must come together to defend our voting rights from increased attacks. ****** Thank you for taking action. This week, Trump spread lies about “election fraud” in Wayne County, which includes part of my congressional district. He’s targeting majority-Black Detroit because he wants to weaken our progressive power. He’s done this before, as part of his attempts to suppress our votes. But we will keep standing up to Trump and fighting for our voting rights, especially as we head toward this November’s general election. I promise to continue fighting for Americans’ needs and rights in Congress. Although the Voting Rights Act has largely been dismantled, we still have the constitutional rights that it was created to enforce. Congress must urgently restore and expand the Voting Rights Act ’s protections by passing new laws. I’m co-sponsoring many policies to defend and expand our right to vote, such as the Fair Representation Act , the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act , the Expanding the VOTE Act , the Universal Right To Vote by Mail Act , the Vote at Home Act , the Time Off to Vote Act , and the Youth Voting Rights Act. Despite the backlash against our progress and attacks on our constitutional rights, our movement is strong and growing larger. And more broadly, the American people are overwhelmingly aligned on many progressive issues. For example, most voters support Medicare for All. Together, we’re pushing our government toward the promise of American democracy — a government of, by, and for the people, where our representatives actually represent us and fight for our needs. Fellow American Patriot,Mike Lindell here, founder of MyPillow and [_**candidate for Minnesota Governor.**_](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=7e4eb9d97dc0437f8a5ee27f14d25ae8&_e=9V20z3mZdrHTm6fuBFlsP06W6QkT4MpSTRPdJsohoziBNnojiAgMmrgddARddYCP767SD4LfNrB_amCGvJvhTUQeO5wyLwoJCYEKMI7xsFupLaqXyKo10xjDITHbx_wvdo3lq_r-rkyRX0gpsHl_3Wcp4J_2v9uX6gvDsZtE4kxo5jRgjJGURFFhRK_VICVBAAw4zRLYnAS1N1lj7JK9kvKExpRnwUTREEAo2-y7yzy7K4mlhZgDdglrGAVoLDy_DlwYa-VPGV_cySIAHQYqoUd0lBXM88kqvNw6NInEpkDlicDhp8gwyA9uO2cvUyNF_7Lq3rEF_rn_ZBtZMAhjwHKSzXmwRASIh3RtmnJik675GvaSjoKeyMwiXHE1XM0dhftjWw_maU_OzEJTGVYQrw%3D%3D) I'm reaching out because this week, I made one of the biggest decisions of my life.After 22 years leading the company I founded, I've stepped down as CEO of MyPillow.I didn't make that decision lightly.For more than two decades, MyPillow has been my life's work. Together, we built a Minnesota company from the ground up, created jobs, and proved that with faith, perseverance, and hard work, incredible things are still possible in this wonderful country.So why would I step away now?[**It's simple: because Minnesota deserves a Governor who is 100% committed.**](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=7e4eb9d97dc0437f8a5ee27f14d25ae8&_e=9V20z3mZdrHTm6fuBFlsP06W6QkT4MpSTRPdJsohoziBNnojiAgMmrgddARddYCP767SD4LfNrB_amCGvJvhTUQeO5wyLwoJCYEKMI7xsFupLaqXyKo10xjDITHbx_wvdo3lq_r-rkyRX0gpsHl_3Wcp4J_2v9uX6gvDsZtE4kxo5jRgjJGURFFhRK_VICVBAAw4zRLYnAS1N1lj7JK9kvKExpRnwUTREEAo2-y7yzy7K4mlhZgDdglrGAVoLDy_vBVe-jdWWfZ9UpUryHb0p8o38a1zCvoUBt-nb-A5dzA9Weu3XfMd9Sl2iKbavrXYegV66m7e_v2QyHgyYL60rPvLBwdyIgL2L5KgsXmu3qlB1CLlkJqHyJcQpOo0cAe17hxLXjbvrUe9VrOFcz9K9Q%3D%3D) Minnesota deserves my complete focus, my full energy, and my undivided attention.I'm all in. 100% -- And today I'm hoping you're all in too.[**Will you click here to make a generous contribution to my campaign to take back our state and make Minnesota Great Again?**](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=7e4eb9d97dc0437f8a5ee27f14d25ae8&_e=9V20z3mZdrHTm6fuBFlsP06W6QkT4MpSTRPdJsohoziBNnojiAgMmrgddARddYCP767SD4LfNrB_amCGvJvhTUQeO5wyLwoJCYEKMI7xsFupLaqXyKo10xjDITHbx_wvdo3lq_r-rkyRX0gpsHl_3Wcp4J_2v9uX6gvDsZtE4kxo5jRgjJGURFFhRK_VICVBAAw4zRLYnAS1N1lj7JK9kvKExpRnwUTREEAo2-y7yzy7K4mlhZgDdglrGAVoLDy_ZOVVL4sosecJipip_eWWmmmeEC2EP3fcYoD8dvyr0Ir8Pbh3RZ8ZJ9CTVYJg2jrIkakZ7UWOqhqsGCn6asmu4tJol1O0tS_b1N6p2YIeGiRnIjDJl2OnpQ0plheUx8uczSdbrMj4Og-c3T2fpe-zMg%3D%3D) My friend, this decision wasn't about walking away. body:
Three years ago, Leaders We Deserve was built around a simple belief.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260809-1&t=1&akid=3846%2E587540%2Es79kRs)
Peter,
**Three years ago,** Leaders We Deserve was built around a simple belief:
The greatest threat to American democracy longterm is not Donald Trump, it is the hopelessness that empowered him. It’s the growing sense that many Americans of all ages — but especially young people — share. A sense that it doesn’t really matter who we vote for because the system doesn’t represent us.
**With Leaders We Deserve we wanted to build an organization that recruited, trained, advised, and funded the best young people our nation has to offer to give a hopeless generation the sense they actually could be properly represented.**
When we started Leaders, it was a big risk. I was just 23 and had graduated from college that spring. When we launched, we didn’t even have enough money to keep the lights on for more than a month. In fact, we were working out of a windowless attic with no air conditioning for much of that first year. But we had faith that people would believe so much in what we were doing that they would make this dream a reality. Thankfully, you and this team came through. We may have been a smaller (and sweatier) team with less resources in the beginning, but we still made so much progress.
**Here are just some of the highlights of the past three years:**
With your help we have played an essential role in electing people like Molly Cook, an abortion rights advocate and ER nurse, to the Texas state Senate. She won _by just 62 votes,_ defeating a Democrat who voted to arm teachers in Texas. Molly just got a maternal healthcare bill passed in her state. We’ve also helped her fund a year round organizing program that has helped secure victories for Texas Democrats up and down the ballot (like 2026 LWD candidate, now Congressman, Christian Menefee in Houston!).
We also helped elect Akbar Ali at just 21 to the Georgia state legislature _by just 153 votes._ Since his election, Akbar has saved Georgia drivers $200 million by cutting the gas tax in the first few months of Trump's Iran war.
At the same time, our other candidate in Georgia, Bryce Berry (elected at 23), played a critical role in blocking Republican redistricting.
We were proud to back Zohran in his primary in the New York mayoral race as one of his largest organizational funders. Since winning, Zohran has made so much progress that I can’t even fit it in this email.
Leaders We Deserve candidates have broken Republican supermajorities in their states, making it possible to win real change, like blocking a bill to arm teachers by just 1 vote.
In 2024, I was elected as a Vice Chair of the DNC. I ran on the idea of offering young voters candidates they could trust and be excited about after we lost them in 2024. When it became clear that the change our party needed was not going to come from within the Democratic establishment, Leaders announced our effort to primary asleep-at-the-wheel Democrats in safe-blue seats who have failed to meet the moment. While we got a ton of flack for it, and it cost me my position at the DNC, it has worked. This term, more members have retired from Congress than at any point in the past 100 years. A new generation is coming into power and young voters are coming back to Democrats. And just last week, we took down our first asleep-at-the-wheel Democratic incumbent of the cycle when our candidate, Donavan McKinney, defeated Shri Thanedar in Michigan’s 13th Congressional District! Now, as we finish out the primary season, we are doing all we can to defeat Republicans with new messengers like Randy Villegas in CA-22 who is running against Republican David Valadao in one of the top Red-to-Blue races of the cycle.
Today on our third birthday, I am writing not only to say thank you but to let you know that due to all your support, our great candidates, and this team, we are in danger of becoming a victim of our own success, and I need your help to make sure that doesn’t happen. Let me explain:
In 2024, our biggest challenge was that young people weren’t running for office because they didn’t see themselves in power. However, now that we have made enormous progress in electing incredible young people, they now see themselves in power and are stepping up to run. The challenge is recruiting the best among them and having the resources to support as many of them as we need to. Don’t get me wrong, this is a good problem to have and I couldn’t be prouder of the progress we've made in just three years. But we need your help now more than ever to continue this generational momentum.
**Here’s the challenge:** Unlike a campaign, our work doesn’t stop after election day. Our most critical work of recruiting candidates is needed most right after November elections, when people are least engaged and fundraising drops because it’s not an election year.
**Here is how you can help:** by donating just **$3 a month** to Leaders We Deserve (or $30, or hey, even $300 if you’re able!). Recurring donors are everything to an organization like ours. They allow our campaigns department to plan out their 2027 State Legislative spends early and endorse more candidates. They give our budget department the confidence to make big campaign investments because they can count on your support the next month. Recurring donors mean I can spend less time fundraising to refill the warchest after the midterms and more time working with our team to recruit and train candidates for 2027. Our recurring donors ensure that we have the stability we need to plan for the next cycle and do everything in our power to win in 2028 by recruiting the best candidates starting in 2027.
So while I have your attention on our third birthday and with just about 90 days to go until Election Day: **[If you can, will you make a $3 or $30 recurring contribution for our third birthday today?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2774?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260809_1_anniv.ODl_uB&refcode=em20260809-3846&amount=3&t=2&akid=3846%2E587540%2Es79kRs)**
_Use the links in this email to start a recurring contribution to Leaders We Deserve._
You are the reason this work is possible, Peter. Because of you, Leaders now has over 260,000 grassroots supporters, 45 endorsed candidates this cycle, 16 full time staff, _and_ an office with air-conditioning!
You were there for me when I needed you most. I am asking for your support now to ensure we continue the momentum and maintain the stability we need to recruit the best candidates possible next cycle. Thank you for believing in this movement and helping us get this far. We truly couldn’t have done it without you.
**Here’s to three years — and everything more we’ll continue to build together.**
So while I have your attention on our third birthday and with just about 90 days to go until Election Day: **[Make a $3 (or $30) monthly contribution now to help us keep up the fight.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2774?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260809_1_anniv.ODl_uB&refcode=em20260809-3846&amount=3&t=3&akid=3846%2E587540%2Es79kRs)**
**[Donate »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2774?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260809_1_anniv.ODl_uB&amount=3&refcode=em20260809-3846&t=22&akid=3846%2E587540%2Es79kRs)**
Thank you,
David Hogg
**P.S. Can’t commit to a monthly donation? That’s okay![Your one-time contribution of $5 goes a long way toward helping us keep up this fight.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260809_1_anniv.4Xsf1D&refcode=em20260809-3846&amount=5&t=23&akid=3846%2E587540%2Es79kRs)**
* * *
**[Donate »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-footer?refcode=em20260809-1&t=24&refcode2=3846_587540_s79kRs&akid=3846%2E587540%2Es79kRs)**
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is a critical way we communicate with grassroots supporters like you. However, if you would like to change your subscription preferences, here are some options:
* [Receive Fewer Emails](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/signup/receive-fewer-emails/?t=25&akid=3846%2E587540%2Es79kRs)
* [Update Your Information](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/signup/update-your-information/)
* [Unsubscribe](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=26&akid=3846%2E587540%2Es79kRs)

To give by check:
Leaders We Deserve
611 Pennsylvania Ave SE
#192
Washington, DC 20003
Email us: [info@leaderswedeserve.com](mailto:info@leaderswedeserve.com)

Hey! It’s Rob Sand, Democratic nominee for Governor of Iowa.

I’m running to be a common-sense Governor for ALL, while my opponent wants
to protect the failed status quo. We have a real shot in this toss-up race
thanks to supporters like you, so I hope you’ll stick around to read this

Don’t mind me, just taking a super

We hosted 8 town halls this week, including in Grundy, Butler, Floyd,

Let me tell you about the luckiest country on Earth, one most people have never even heard of. Guyana is a former British colony on the northern coast of South America with a population of **800,000 people** , fewer than Austin, Texas. In 2015, ExxonMobil was drilling in the waters off Georgetown, Guyana and struck oil. What they found was staggering: [over 11 billion barrels of recoverable resources](https://substack.com/redirect/ce39bcd0-4ca5-4635-8bf9-2a949b46d7dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the Stabroek Block, one of the largest discoveries of the 21st century. In just 11 years, Guyana went from [zero to 903,000 barrels per day](https://substack.com/redirect/90d06036-ef2c-4d52-9849-46bf46441683?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), one of the fastest production ramp-ups in the history of global oil.
The numbers are staggering. Guyana has been and continues to be the [fastest-growing economy on Earth](https://substack.com/redirect/a1265af0-ea52-418a-9222-2bb260aae423?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), with GDP growth of **43.6% in 2024, 19.3% in 2025, and a projected 16.2% in 2026**. It is now the [11th richest country in the world by GDP per capita](https://substack.com/redirect/90d06036-ef2c-4d52-9849-46bf46441683?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The government has taken in [$6.2 billion in oil revenues](https://substack.com/redirect/a1265af0-ea52-418a-9222-2bb260aae423?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as of late 2024, and this year's annual revenue is projected to exceed $3 billion. A fifth offshore project, the [$12.7 billion Uaru development](https://substack.com/redirect/373ffbe9-74e6-400c-8534-ba11f40cc0ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), comes online this year, which will drive production past one million barrels per day. By 2030, Guyana could be pumping [1.9 million barrels per day](https://substack.com/redirect/373ffbe9-74e6-400c-8534-ba11f40cc0ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), becoming South America's second-largest producer behind Brazil (and ahead of Venezuela).

The main reason for my concern about this potential conflict was a referendum held by the Government of Venezuela that called for declaring sovereignty over more than two-thirds of Guyana's land in a region known as the Ess...](https://substack.com/redirect/61151182-7ee5-434e-8615-0a05388cb22c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

---](https://substack.com/redirect/61151182-7ee5-434e-8615-0a05388cb22c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
And the timing couldn't be better. With the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed by the Iran war, the world is desperate for oil that doesn't pass through a chokepoint. Guyana's crude ships straight across the Atlantic to the US Gulf Coast...no Suez, no Hormuz, no Malacca. [US imports from Guyana hit 261,000 barrels per day in April](https://substack.com/redirect/373ffbe9-74e6-400c-8534-ba11f40cc0ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg); that's up 51% in just two years.
Think about it. Guyana is a country of 800,000 people, sitting on 11 billion barrels, growing at 20% a year, with no chokepoint risk, at a moment when the world's most important shipping lane is closed. What would you call that? The luckiest country on Earth. But like all coins, however, there are two sides. Lucky, yes. But also cursed.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/a8e639c1-a91e-4c3a-afb5-451a38fd105b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
To begin, there's the neighborhood. Venezuela claims sovereignty over **two-thirds of Guyana 's territory**, specifically the Essequibo region, a chunk of land roughly the size of Georgia. In 2023, Caracas held a referendum on annexing it. In 2024, Maduro signed the annexation into law. The disputed territory, surprise surprise, happens to contain the waters where all of Guyana's oil is being extracted.
The case is now before the International Court of Justice, but here's the uncomfortable reality. The claim isn't a remnant of Maduro's idiosyncratic rule. It commands rare consensus across Venezuela's political spectrum, _including the opposition_. Regime change won't extinguish the territorial dispute, which goes back decades. A post-Maduro government seeking legitimacy could even find nationalist utility in pressing the claim harder.
* * *
## [Is War Coming to South America?](https://substack.com/redirect/4f34ba66-3bae-4aee-b41f-a5a66a4eaaf4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [Vikram Mansharamani](https://substack.com/profile/37278065-vikram-mansharamani)| | *
---|---|---
| December 4, 2023
[](https://substack.com/redirect/4f34ba66-3bae-4aee-b41f-a5a66a4eaaf4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Failed socialist policies in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela destroyed South America's most prosperous country and created economic hardship for most of the country. Hyperinflation decimated the purchasing power of ordinary citizens and led to extreme shortages of many household items, ranging from toilet paper to](https://substack.com/redirect/4f34ba66-3bae-4aee-b41f-a5a66a4eaaf4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/4f34ba66-3bae-4aee-b41f-a5a66a4eaaf4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
But there's also the traditional resource curse known as [Dutch Disease](https://substack.com/redirect/115d08be-9c0b-4a22-b1de-3d9ed22315c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The condition, repeated across decades and continents, is one in which oil wealth destroys the very economies it enriches. For Dutch Disease to take root, a country must be early in its development of institutions, lack checks and balances, and exhibit **high inequality** , among other conditions.
Last week, [Bloomberg Opinion](https://substack.com/redirect/04354384-8b60-42bf-9427-2925b8b484be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) published an analysis titled "Oil's Curse Is Hanging Over the World's Fastest-Growing Economy," and its conclusions were damning. Guyana, Bloomberg found, is fertile ground for Dutch Disease. The country, Bloomberg noted, exhibits **weak institutions, inadequate transparency, widening inequality, and political power concentrated around the state**. The production-sharing agreement with ExxonMobil has been criticized as lopsided. $214 million in disputed audit costs remain unresolved five years after being flagged. Procurement is opaque. Decision-making is concentrated in a handful of officials.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..1cuChgTXgtxILRWTiYp9bXNfG0VTZm_rdfMuHeEExFU?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=210395510)
And then there's the income inequality, which creates a risk of instability. Despite being the 11th richest country in the world by GDP per capita, [58% of Guyana's population still lives in poverty](https://substack.com/redirect/ce39bcd0-4ca5-4635-8bf9-2a949b46d7dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). GDP is breaking records, the sovereign wealth fund is swelling, and yet most Guyanese endure unreliable electricity, inadequate healthcare, poor drainage, rising food prices, and housing shortages. The oil boom is real and there's no question wealth is being generated. Whether it trickles down to the ordinary citizens is an entirely different question. The risk of unrest is rising.
And then, like most things in the world these days, there's China. The ExxonMobil consortium that controls the Stabroek Block includes [China's National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC) as a 25% economic partner](https://substack.com/redirect/a1265af0-ea52-418a-9222-2bb260aae423?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). A quarter of the biggest oil play in the Western Hemisphere is owned by Beijing. With Washington, DC pushing a 21st century version of the Monroe-Doctrine and intent on getting everyone out of its neighborhood, China is already inside the deal.
* * *
## [A Coherent US National Security Strategy](https://substack.com/redirect/c705f49c-b803-4921-90f4-f1fa516b3843?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---

| December 8, 2025
[](https://substack.com/redirect/c705f49c-b803-4921-90f4-f1fa516b3843?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Regular readers of my work know that I have been closely watching America's foreign policy during Trump's second term. While others saw incoherence or contradictions - destroying drug boats in the Caribbean but not those of the Houthi's in the Red Sea, pulling back from much of the world while getting more engaged in South America, moving on from the Wa...](https://substack.com/redirect/c705f49c-b803-4921-90f4-f1fa516b3843?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* * *
So, Guyana is both lucky and cursed...but how might this contradiction resolve itself? Readers will know that I deal in probabilistic scenarios rather than predictions, and I see two paths. Guyana's president says he wants to follow the ["Norway model"](https://substack.com/redirect/2c0921f0-26dc-42e1-a643-038e02f72d19?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), that is to say, using oil wealth to build lasting prosperity through a well-managed sovereign fund, infrastructure, and economic diversification. But Norway had 150 years of democratic institutions before it struck oil; Guyana has had seven. Venezuela said the same thing once, and Nigeria, and Angola...and that's the second possible outcome. The same path as these failed states.
The luckiest country on Earth has 11 billion barrels of oil, the fastest-growing economy in the world, and a neighbor that claims two-thirds of its land. It has $3 billion a year in revenue flowing in and 58% of its people living in poverty. It has the Norway model as its aspiration and the Venezuela model next door as its warning.
Luck is not a strategy. And oil, as every petrostate eventually learns, is not a blessing until you prove it isn't a curse.

I’ve spent plenty of time on the road recently traveling the Commonwealth as my campaign gears up for the general election. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136921472/639042178/1079622208?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_OnTheRoad_260809_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5NzZjZmI2Mi0wYjk0LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=zBz2AUKI57zEfwfXo_GJYatEKHbofmp-jFPhocaGVmg=) And no matter where I go, I hear the same frustration and concern. I've got to tell you, folks are not shy about telling me what's on their minds.

At every single stop, I’ve heard from a Virginian struggling to face rising prices. Groceries. Rent. Utilities. Child care. They can tell you what the squeeze costs them down to the dollar.

No matter the city, I’ve heard from folks whose insurance premiums have skyrocketed this year after Republicans let Obamacare tax credits expire while handing out tax cuts to the wealthiest few.

Not to mention the enormous concerns I’ve heard about the impact of data centers on Virginia communities and our utility bills. People are worried about how these data centers and artificial intelligence are going to affect our communities, about the lack of transparency in their power and water usage, about what they’ll do to good-paying jobs. It’s why I’ve introduced multiple bills to hold large tech accountable and start preparing our workforce for the economy of the future.

**But here's the other thing I'm seeing, Derek, and it's the part that keeps me going:**

Folks are showing up to volunteer, asking their friends and family to get involved, and helping my campaign get the resources we need for a winning get-out-the-vote operation.

**I have not seen this kind of energy in Virginia in a long time.**

Virginia voters understand what's at stake – now we need to turn this energy and momentum into votes. And with 86 days until Election Day, we’re running out of time.

[_**That’s why I’m asking: will you chip in right now to keep this campaign on the road, help us reach voters across Virginia, and keep up our fight for a better future?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136921473/639042179/1079622208?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_OnTheRoad_260809_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5NzZjZmI2Mi0wYjk0LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=zBz2AUKI57zEfwfXo_GJYatEKHbofmp-jFPhocaGVmg=)

name: Kirk Cameron
subject: The Christian response to drag queen story hour
body:
| [View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6538405/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvUFRBZGd1dnVUaA/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA4MDk/LbmNseWdCU1JtQQ/qP2hpZHM9bmMwWnJTM005SEJYNnhscw/ganipiQ/sfj40c59aee)
| | | If you haven’t heard about the “See You at the Library Day” on Fox News or Newsmax or your other favorite news sources, please let me tell you why it’s so critical.
---
| | Fellow Conservative, If you haven’t heard about “See You at the Library Day” on Fox News or Newsmax or your other favorite news sources, _**[please let me tell you why it’s so critical.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**_ Back when you were growing up, you may remember lazy Saturdays at the library with a kind but stern librarian. She would fill your mind with classics like _Pat the Bunny_ and _The Little Engine That Could_. And eventually you got old enough to roam by yourself and discover adventures like the _Three Musketeers_ , _Treasure Island_ and _Charlotte’s Web_. But today, all that has changed. Instead of filling children with wholesome stories, the president of the American Library Association (ALA) says libraries should be used to address ‘systemic racism’ and elevate ‘BIPOC and GLBTQR+ writers and voices.’ Radical librarians call _Adventures of Huckleberry Finn_ and _To Kill a Mockingbird_ “racist.” They’ve stripped Laura Ingalls Wilder’s name from a prestigious book award because of her “problematic’ _Little House_ series. And they bring in men wearing full makeup, dresses, and high heels for “Drag Queen Story Hours” where books like these are read to children of all ages... _A is for Activist._ An _ABC_ _board_ _book_ for “families who want their kids to grow up in a space that is unapologetic about activism, environmental justice, civil rights, LGBTQ rights, and everything else that activists believe in and fight for.” _Woke Baby_. “For all the littlest progressives, waking up to seize a new day of justice and activism. Woke babies raise their fists in the air. Woke babies cry out for justice. Woke babies grow up to change the world.” _Prince and Knight._ The “premier queer-friendly fairy tale” about a prince who marries a knight instead of a princess. And _The Hips on the Drag Queens Go Swish, Swish, Swish._ A “family-friendly celebration of drag” that encourages children to “work it.” I wish I could tell you this was only happening in places like New York City and San Francisco...
---
| | [ ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
| | ...but that’s just not true. <\- THIS IS A MAN leading “Drag Queen Story Hour.”
---
| | _**[That’s why parents and grandparents across the country are rising up through See You At The Library Day.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**_ For decades, the ultra-liberal Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation and George Soros’ Open Society have spent millions radicalizing the ALA. And as a result, a new generation of pink-haired, activist librarians have made it their mission to fill library shelves with anti-American, LGBTQ-friendly, and explicitly sexual content. Maybe you’ve noticed all the displays at your own library celebrating Pride Month or elevating ‘the environment’ to a type of religion. Or maybe you’ve noticed the “Teen Zone” which is really meant to be a “parent-free” zone. The “Teen Zone” is filled with books like: _Rick_ about a cross-dressing Grandpa, _Melissa_ filled with graphic nudity, and _Darkstalker_ featuring gory violence and domestic abuse. But here’s what’s really alarming. We can’t just sit back and say, “Well, I’ll just make sure my family doesn’t go to “Drag Queen Story Hour” and we won’t check out those inappropriate books.” That may be good for your family -- for now. But meanwhile, the ALA uses our taxpayer-funded libraries to lure in millions of _other_ children who grow up to be the very activists who are destroying our country and conservative values! _**[I hope you see why I need your help today.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.) **_ My name is Kirk Cameron. Maybe you recognize me from the 1980’s family sitcom “Growing Pains” or from my work in inspirational movies like “Fireproof” and “Left Behind.” I know firsthand how dangerous it is to be indoctrinated by leftist values. Pride almost took me down as a young actor in Hollywood. But the gospel saved me. I love being an actor, but what’s far more important is being a husband, dad, grandad, and a Christian. When I saw what book publishers and libraries were doing to indoctrinate children with anti-God, anti-family, anti-America messages, I knew I had a duty to take action. So, I wrote a little book called “As You Grow” to teach children how to grow in wisdom through the fruit of the spirit. Then I decided to go one step further and counter those awful “Drag Queen Story Hours” with _conservative Story Hours_ filled with the classic books you and I grew up with, plus new wholesome books like mine that captivate children with lessons in bravery, honesty, kindness, and patriotism. And boy, the ALA and radical librarians didn’t like that one bit. >> Over 50 libraries rejected my request to host our Story Hour. >> The ALA helped local libraries scheme ways to keep me out including booking all the event rooms for themselves. >> Social media blew up with attacks: I was compared to a Nazi (that’s original), my publisher was accused of trying to “confuse and demoralize children,” supporters were described as “bored moms/busybodies who need something to feel good about,” and on and on. I can’t even print most things these radicals said because it’s so vile. In the end I got two libraries to reverse course by reminding them that their censorship violated the Constitution of the United States. And thousands of parents and grandparents brought their little ones to those “Story Hours” where we pledged allegiance to the flag, sang “God Bless America”, and read wholesome and Godly books. It was incredible. But here’s the greatest part... From there, parents and grandparents started asking how they could host “Story Hours” of their own. And that’s how the nationwide “See You at the Library” movement was born. Last year, committed conservatives just like you booked event rooms at 201 libraries in 46 states. On the same day, across America hundreds of “Story Hours” filled children’s hearts with goodness, gratitude, and God. Conservative parents, grandparents, and patriots stood together for a very simple mission -- to reject the Left’s radical ideas and reclaim childhood innocence in America’s libraries. _**[And this year, honoring America’s 250th birthday, my ambitious goal is to expand “See You at the Library Day” to reach 250,000 children.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**_ The exact date will soon be announced. And before then, I need you! The response from parents, grandparents, and patriots who want to host “Story Hours” has been overwhelming. That’s a very good thing. But it’s going to be a big undertaking and expensive to give these volunteers the resources they need to hold “Story Hours” for 250,000 children. _**[That’s why I’ve teamed with a very special non-profit called BRAVE for Good to make this year’s “See You at the Library Day” a bigger success than ever.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**_ **BRAVE for Good** was started by BRAVE Books -- the small Christian publisher of my book “As You Grow” –- because so many patriots were asking how they could help “See You at the Library Day” with a tax-deductible gift. Your sponsorship gift helps send a ‘Story Hour Kit’ to every parent, grandparent, and patriot who’s organizing a “See You at the Library” event. The kit includes everything they need to bring your conservative values back into our public libraries: instructions for booking their library space and running their Story Hour, small American flags for little ones, fun stickers, wholesome books, Bible memory verse cards, and other specialty items. Your sponsorship gift is the only way we can fund our “Story Hours” for 250,000 children to counter the radical leftists who’ve taken control of our libraries. We don’t have the millions behind us like the giant taxpayer-funded ALA. _**[Knowing that, please consider a sponsorship gift of $125. That’s enough to sponsor one entire ‘Story Hour Kit’ yourself.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**_ Singlehandedly, you’ll be reaching 50 children with our wholesome, Godly, and patriotic message. Whatever you can give whether it’s $35, $125, or anything higher or lower please send in your sponsorship gift in the next 48 hours so we know how many libraries we have sponsored for this year’s “See You at the Library Day.”
---
[ **DONATE** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Thank you! God Bless You and God Bless America,
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Kirk Cameron
---
|
---
| | [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
**BRAVE For Good** 100 I-45 N 260 Conroe, TX 77301
---

Alexandria, VA 22314

name: The Democratic National Committee
subject: We’re trying something totally different.
body:
---
Derek, You’ve probably seen a lot of stories about our finances this cycle, and we want you to know that it’s true: The RNC has an 8-1 cash advantage on us right now. The conventional wisdom is to raise and hoard money, so that you can spend it all in the last few weeks. But that strategy has failed too many times, **so we're trying something totally different.** Last year, Republicans were collecting contributions from conservative billionaires to hoard in their massive war chests. Instead, we chose to make unprecedented investments in key races, state parties, and organizing infrastructure to support Democrats running for office. We didn’t have the money to pay for it yet, but we were confident that we’d see big returns at the ballot box. And that’s exactly what’s been happening. Democrats have won or overperformed in 271 of 303 key elections since Trump took office, and we’re on track to see an even bigger blue wave this November. **So yes, we have less cash on hand than our billionaire-funded MAGA counterparts.** But that’s because we know the stakes of this election. We know that we can’t afford to wake up on November 4th with regrets. So we’re doing everything we can to ensure a resounding victory this year — including investing early and often in key races, instead of waiting around and watching the number on our bank statements tick up. You might not know this, Derek, but 99.7% of our contributions come from grassroots supporters just like you stepping up and giving what they can. _You_ are the reason we’ve been able to make these investments. So we have to ask: [**Will you chip in $7 to power Democrats across the country to victory? Big primary wins, high-stakes races, and Big Oil's latest cash grab.

---
Welcome to the August edition of **_The JanePAC Monthly_**. We're now less than three months from Election Day, and our movement is hitting its stride. Primary wins are stacking up, critical races are heating up, and Big Oil is spending big to stop us. But we've never been more ready for the fight. Let's dive in! 👇
* * *
**A BIG PRIMARY NIGHT FOR OUR CLIMATE CHAMPIONS** JanePAC leaders delivered major victories in Michigan this week — proving once again that grassroots power can win up and down the ballot. | **MICHIGAN WINS**
---
In Michigan, climate champions **William Lawrence in MI-07** and **Donavan McKinney in MI-13** won their Democratic primaries, bringing us one step closer to flipping the House in November.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136924473/639050442/2105508926?refcode=ea.35a854b4-0f94-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ms=ea.35a854b4-0f94-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjM1YTg1NGI0LTBmOTQtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMGQzYTExZmEzMCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=7gsZJgdjmN54Ji5r3fnzn3j2vfDa_fK3Kh04rA41zuI=)
Special interests spent millions trying to stop these candidates, but Michigan voters made one thing clear: Big Oil does not get the final say.
And the wins didn’t stop there. We need to build a firewall at the state level to stop Trump’s giveaways to Big Polluters _and_ his authoritarian attacks on our neighbors. JanePAC climate champions **Chris Gilmer-Hill, Kimberly Edwards, Dylan Wegela, and Natalie Price advanced in their races for the Michigan Legislature. Each of them represents a brick of the firewall that will save our planet.**
* * *
**⚖️ THE CLIMATE CASE TO WATCH THIS FALL**
**This fall, the Supreme Court will hear arguments from oil giants ExxonMobil and Suncor Energy about why they should avoid trial** in one of dozens of lawsuits accusing fossil fuel companies of misleading the public about climate change and the dangers associated with fossil fuels for decades.
The City and County of Boulder, Colorado, is suing these two oil companies, and argues that they should help pay for the mounting costs of local climate damage. **One report estimates that climate change could cost Colorado communities as much as $37 billion by 2050.**
But the justices have added an unexpected wrinkle: whether the Supreme Court should even intervene at this stage of the case. Some legal experts see that question as a sign that the Court may be more divided than Big Oil was counting on.
The outcome could shape whether communities across the country can hold fossil fuel companies accountable for the damage they helped cause.
