clean_body: Big primary wins, high-stakes races, and Big Oil's latest cash grab. | Welcome to the August edition of The JanePAC Monthly. We're now less than three months from Election Day, and our movement is hitting its stride. Primary wins are stacking up, critical races are heating up, and Big Oil is spending big to stop us. But we've never been more ready for the fight. Let's dive in! 👇 A BIG PRIMARY NIGHT FOR OUR CLIMATE CHAMPIONS JanePAC leaders delivered major victories in Michigan this week — proving once again that grassroots power can win up and down the ballot. | MICHIGAN WINS In Michigan, climate champions William Lawrence in MI-07 and Donavan McKinney in MI-13 won their Democratic primaries, bringing us one step closer to flipping the House in November. = Special interests spent millions trying to stop these candidates, but Michigan voters made one thing clear: Big Oil does not get the final say. And the wins didn’t stop there. We need to build a firewall at the state level to stop Trump’s giveaways to Big Polluters and his authoritarian attacks on our neighbors. JanePAC climate champions Chris Gilmer-Hill, Kimberly Edwards, Dylan Wegela, and Natalie Price advanced in their races for the Michigan Legislature. Each of them represents a brick of the firewall that will save our planet. ⚖️ THE CLIMATE CASE TO WATCH THIS FALL This fall, the Supreme Court will hear arguments from oil giants ExxonMobil and Suncor Energy about why they should avoid trial in one of dozens of lawsuits accusing fossil fuel companies of misleading the public about climate change and the dangers associated with fossil fuels for decades. The City and County of Boulder, Colorado, is suing these two oil companies, and argues that they should help pay for the mounting costs of local climate damage. One report estimates that climate change could cost Colorado communities as much as $37 billion by 2050. But the justices have added an unexpected wrinkle: whether the Supreme Court should even intervene at this stage of the case. Some legal experts see that question as a sign that the Court may be more divided than Big Oil was counting on. The outcome could shape whether communities across the country can hold fossil fuel companies accountable for the damage they helped cause. 🗳️ WEEKEND READING: PEGGY FLANAGAN FACES A DEFINING TEST IN MINNESOTA On Tuesday, Minnesota voters will cast their ballots in what could become the bellwether race of 2026 — and JanePAC-endorsed Lt. Gov. body:
I’m not sending this message to millions of people.
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=8182%2E582294%2EtLfqzl)
I know my team and I email you a lot to share updates about our campaign.
But today’s message is a little bit different. Let me tell you why:
Right now I’m only reaching out to _a smaller group of people like you_ – **people who have yet to make their first-ever donation to our campaign.**
I’m specifically emailing folks like you to ask for a big favor. With the GOP outspending us, I’m counting on your help in a major way.
**[Will you make your very first $5 donation to help us close the gap? We must raise $200,000 in order to keep pace with the massive flood of GOP spending coming into our state if we want a shot at flipping the Senate.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260809_2.jNdI5j&refcode=em20260809-2&t=2&akid=8182%2E582294%2EtLfqzl)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260809_2.jNdI5j&amount=5&refcode=em20260809-2&t=21&akid=8182%2E582294%2EtLfqzl)**
Before I sat down to write this email, my team made sure I knew this about you:
According to our records, you have an opportunity to make TODAY the very first day you contribute to our campaign. Every donation – even a couple bucks – makes a difference in our fight to keep New Hampshire’s Senate seat, and **I’m relying on a few more first-time donors to step up.**
None of this is possible without you. **[So I’m asking you to consider making your first-ever $5 donation today. Every dollar we raise will help us close the gap and prove to the GOP that New Hampshire is not for sale.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260809_2.jNdI5j&refcode=em20260809-2&t=22&akid=8182%2E582294%2EtLfqzl)**
Thank you,
Chris Pappas
**New Hampshire is poised to be one of the closest Senate races in the country. Will you chip in today to help Chris stop the Republicans from flipping the Granite State red and expanding their Senate majority?**
**[Donate »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_cp_footer?refcode=em20260809-2&t=23&refcode2=8182_582294_tLfqzl&akid=8182%2E582294%2EtLfqzl)**
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is a critical way we communicate with grassroots supporters like you. However, if you would like to change your subscription preferences, here are some options:

Less than 90 days.
That's how long until Election Day — and how long we have to build the majority that stops Donald Trump's MAGA agenda.
At Equal Opportunity Now, we're not waiting until October to get serious. We're supporting Democrats up and down the ballot right now — congressional candidates in the tightest battlegrounds in America, state legislative candidates in districts nobody's watching, and the local leaders who will be the bench of this party for the next twenty years.
Will you chip in $25 or $50 today to help us fund the fighters running to take on Trump and his allies? With less than 90 days until Election Day, every moment and every dollar counts. » [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email?amount=25]

Fellow American Patriot, Mike Lindell here, founder of MyPillow and [_**candidate for Minnesota Governor.**_](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjN9AAwAAAAAAj2I1QYPNlr_J6DbANymaCUJoTukbYtz3Jj5KzSnv0hKI20Mf8ZW5duxqYVFB8hVTcALIciBC8H5n3h9sA6A71c3Xo6DmZQfdGDvxA-i) I'm reaching out because this week, I made one of the biggest decisions of my life. After 22 years leading the company I founded, I've stepped down as CEO of MyPillow. I didn't make that decision lightly. For more than two decades, MyPillow has been my life's work. Together, we built a Minnesota company from the ground up, created jobs, and proved that with faith, perseverance, and hard work, incredible things are still possible in this wonderful country.So why would I step away now?[**It's simple: because Minnesota deserves a Governor who is 100% committed.** ](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjN9AAwAAAAAAj2I1QYQyScW0xJ7xlvKu9qblqyH6_zfNR3-NvLgiSoLykwDbGaBW6yDslemogWujDXsMPZvt7RTqeyM6f4NMGKnMe4SNrwLGTH0d4a-)Minnesota deserves my complete focus, my full energy, and my undivided attention.I'm all in. 100% -- And today I'm hoping you're all in too.[**Will you click here to make a generous contribution to my campaign to take back our state and make Minnesota Great Again?**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjN9AAwAAAAAAj2I1QYRDdi4cPR4WNf5ERCLJtCtlhWJYvWzhf3Po7OvnXRTjtszJep41HGafnBw2f4CpcOFoSPlWomh9Pf3LtXjJ8O0UqGPoOy2vOeW) My friend, this decision wasn't about walking away. It's about stepping up for you. Career politicians spend their lives protecting what's best for themselves. They worry about their next title, their next election, and their next opportunity.I'm choosing a different path. I'm putting Minnesota ahead of myself. I'm choosing the fight to save Minnesota and I'm giving it my all. I don't have a backup plan. I'm all in. President Trump honored me with his endorsement because he knows I'll fight for Minnesota without compromise. Now I'm backing up those words and his confidence with action by giving 100% to this campaign. But I can't do it by myself. **[I need grassroots conservatives across Minnesota-and across the country-standing with me.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjN9AAwAAAAAAj2I1QYSTMXBApR4m-5b4zvCy5XHrJbLTfC91L1zax7HBlWHfXluNqnfBI9iS6Dx_fhaw5xsrTcsICt89vVG337ggQ0DyrjjN46_YWIz)** _**_Every phone call we make..._**_ _**_Every yard sign we print..._**_ _**_Every door we knock..._**_ _**_Every voter we reach..._**_ It's only possible because people like you decide this campaign is worth fighting for. **If you believe Minnesota deserves a Governor who's willing to sacrifice, willing to lead, and willing to put our state first, I'm asking you to stand with me today.** **[Will you make a contribution of $10, $25, $50, or whatever you can afford to help me win this race?](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjN9AAwAAAAAAj2I1QYTBdbUt8DEe4MKG98DpdhGs9z6BNyJ1MvCySIAUP7khNHnHFRw2boHO25ujlxXVTcgIdoN2edeoIQo6MsYiwnQ1vdeTXEBfAWM)** **_Together, we can save Minnesota._** **_I'm all in. I hope you'll be all in with me._**
---
| | | Thank you, and God bless.
---
**Mike Lindell,** _**Republican Candidate for Governor**_

| | The Pentagon just quietly updated its war casualty database. The number of American servicemembers injured or killed in Trump's war is now over 600. This comes just days after the administration tried to erase troop deaths from its own website. **Trump's failed war is costing us dearly, in lives and in dollars, and he's hoping you won't notice.** I'm holding in my heart the families and loved ones of the servicemembers killed and injured, and I haven't forgotten the Iranian civilians who have died in this war, too. _Every single one of these losses was avoidable._ The Constitution is clear: the power to declare war belongs to Congress, not the President. But Trump ignored the law, risked servicemembers' lives, and now he's trying to hide the cost from the American people. We've seen where this leads. Endless wars. Lost lives. Costs skyrocketing. Billions of taxpayer dollars spent with no clear plan and no oversight. name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: The disturbing reality of immigration detention
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
I joined Rep. Ilhan Omar to conduct oversight at an ICE facility—and what we found demands answers.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260809-6575-footer&t=1&akid=6575%2E420207%2EMHR_6g)
Peter,
I recently joined Congresswoman Ilhan Omar to conduct congressional oversight at an ICE detention facility in Minnesota.
We went because the American people deserve to know what is happening behind those walls — and because every person, regardless of their immigration status, deserves to be treated with dignity and humanity.
**What we found was deeply disturbing:**
* We were not allowed to speak with the people being detained. In fact, we were required to sign paperwork agreeing that we would not interact with them.

* When we asked simple questions regarding training and policy, we were met with hostility from agents.

* Inside, I saw people being held in leg restraints — a practice that is far from routine.

* We also learned that dozens of people were being transported for deportation while families and communities were left in the dark.

This is exactly why congressional oversight is so important.
**_No_ agency should be able to operate without accountability. No one should be deprived of their dignity behind closed doors while the public is kept in the dark.**
I have never stopped fighting to hold ICE accountable, demand transparency, and push for an immigration system rooted in _humanity_ instead of fear. That work didn't begin with this visit, and it certainly won't end here.
But taking on an administration determined to expand detention and deportation isn't easy. **It requires people across the country standing together and refusing to look away.**
[**If you're able, will you make a contribution of $3 today to help me continue holding ICE accountable, defending immigrant communities, and fighting for a more just immigration system?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260809-1.ixf1no&refcode=em20260809-6575&amount=3&t=2&akid=6575%2E420207%2EMHR_6g)

In solidarity,

Fellow Patriot - I'm not a politician. In fact, I've never run for office before.

I never expected to be running for office. I have never had any desire to be a politician. I am doing this because I am answering President Donald Trump's call to serve and want to stand up for South Carolina and fight for his agenda.

_**Like Lindsey, I am a hard worker with a servant's heart.**_ We grew up in the back of a bar and liquor store, in one room. Our parents worked hard every day to make ends meet - there was no time for sickness and few vacations, because if the doors weren't open, no money was coming in.

What I've spent my life doing is serving South Carolina - including running a state agency with 130 employees and a $90 million budget. We turned it from a struggling organization into a national model helping people find work and live independently. We made sure all spending was reasonable, allowable, and necessary. _I fought against duplication of services, knowing it wasted taxpayers' dollars_.

clean_body: I am answering President Donald Trump's call to serve and want to stand up for South Carolina and fight for his agenda. | Fellow Patriot - I'm not a politician. In fact, I've never run for office before. I never expected to be running for office. I have never had any desire to be a politician. I am doing this because I am answering President Donald Trump's call to serve and want to stand up for South Carolina and fight for his agenda. Like Lindsey, I am a hard worker with a servant's heart. We grew up in the back of a bar and liquor store, in one room. Our parents worked hard every day to make ends meet - there was no time for sickness and few vacations, because if the doors weren't open, no money was coming in. What I've spent my life doing is serving South Carolina - including running a state agency with 130 employees and a $90 million budget. We turned it from a struggling organization into a national model helping people find work and live independently. We made sure all spending was reasonable, allowable, and necessary. I fought against duplication of services, knowing it wasted taxpayers' dollars. I'm a mother, a grandmother, and a wife, and now South Carolina's first female United States Senator, I know how to bargain shop, and I look for the buy-one-get-one-free sales at the grocery store. I just bought a new pair of shoes to walk around the U.S. Capitol off the clearance rack at the Shoe Warehouse. I cut my own grass with a push mower, and yes, I know how to use a weed eater. I support the Right to Life. I believe in showing ID to vote to save our country. I oppose DEI. I think AOC is C-R-A-Z-Y. I think Anthony Fauci should stop staring at the floor and answer the questions. I stand for the national anthem. I believe our veterans are heroes. I will always Back the Blue. And I know that President Trump and I will Make America Great Again. I am the first woman United States senator in South Carolina history. My Democratic opponent, Dr. Annie Andrews, must not be the second. She supports turning confused little boys into little girls and vice versa. I believe that makes her the worst pediatrician in the country. President Trump wants a fighter in the Senate. That's exactly why he's in my corner in this race. Thanks, Darline Graham P.S. In 1988, a woman from Globe, Arizona made history. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136930007/639063856/-1017980171?refcode=AU_AZD_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260809_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS8xMDU1MTYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNmRhZWE5MjYtMWM5NC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAwZDNhMTFmYTMwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=vZHY-TQmTOsqvJx0Esg8D8N_k5E3B4_MAcTNSpKW7vM=) Rose Mofford, born the child of Croatian immigrants, a standout athlete and high school valedictorian — became Arizona's first female governor. In doing so, she paved the way for Arizona to lead the nation with more women governors than any other state in American history. She served with heart and determination, and put the needs of Arizona's most vulnerable citizens first. She was a Democrat in a deeply Republican state, and she was beloved by both parties because she never stopped showing up for the people of Arizona. Rose Mofford didn't set out to be a role model. She became one anyway. Last month, Arizona Democratic women followed in her footsteps, and then some. Women are 75% of Arizona's Democratic U.S. House nominees — six of eight — while zero of nine Republican nominees are women. Incumbent Attorney General Kris Mayes sailed through her primary unopposed, ready to defend Arizona's democracy against whatever Republicans throw at us in November. Governor Katie Hobbs is running for a second term and a chance to deliver the first Democratic trifecta in 60 years. Dr. Teresa Leyba Ruiz — the only Superintendent of Public Instruction candidate who is also a certified teacher — won her primary in a historic blowout, and is now headed to November to fight for Arizona's students and educators. And JoAnna Mendoza — a former Marine Corps drill instructor and working mom — is our nominee in one of the most competitive congressional races in the country. The contrast couldn't be starker. Zero of nine Republican U.S. House nominees in Arizona are women. Not one. Arizona Democratic women are on the ballot, in the fight, and ready to win. And the Arizona Democratic Party is behind every single one of them — organizing in all 15 counties, building the infrastructure to turn out voters, and making sure that the women who are carrying our banner into November have every resource they need to win. That's the legacy Rose Mofford left us. And we intend to honor it. She served with heart and determination, and put the needs of Arizona's most vulnerable citizens first. She was a Democrat in a deeply Republican state, and she was beloved by both parties because she never stopped showing up for the people of Arizona. Rose Mofford didn't set out to be a role model. She became one anyway. Last month, Arizona Democratic women followed in her footsteps, and then some. Women are 75% of Arizona's Democratic U.S. House nominees — six of eight — while zero of nine Republican nominees are women. Incumbent Attorney General Kris Mayes sailed through her primary unopposed, ready to defend Arizona's democracy against whatever Republicans throw at us in November. Governor Katie Hobbs is running for a second term and a chance to deliver the first Democratic trifecta in 60 years. Dr. Teresa Leyba Ruiz — the only Superintendent of Public Instruction candidate who is also a certified teacher — won her primary in a historic blowout, and is now headed to November to fight for Arizona's students and educators. And JoAnna Mendoza — a former Marine Corps drill instructor and working mom — is our nominee in one of the most competitive congressional races in the country. The contrast couldn't be starker. Zero of nine Republican U.S. House nominees in Arizona are women. Not one. Arizona Democratic women are on the ballot, in the fight, and ready to win. And the Arizona Democratic Party is behind every single one of them — organizing in all 15 counties, building the infrastructure to turn out voters, and making sure that the women who are carrying our banner into November have every resource they need to win. That's the legacy Rose Mofford left us. And we intend to honor it. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | = = | = = | = = Rose Mofford broke the glass ceiling. Now we're shattering it. Hey folks,
New Mexico's attorney general is suing the DOJ for access to the unredacted Epstein files as part of the state's investigation into Zorro Ranch. At the same time, Katie Phang's legal fight for additional Epstein records just scored an important win. The pressure is building, and we cannot stop paying attention.
* [**00:00:49**] New Mexico's attorney general sues the DOJ, demanding unredacted Epstein records connected to the investigation into Zorro Ranch.
* [**00:02:45**] The lawsuit accuses the DOJ of unlawfully withholding records New Mexico says are essential to pursuing accountability for victims and survivors.
* [**00:05:04**] Katie Phang's separate legal battle enters the picture--and a federal judge demands answers about withheld handwritten FBI interview notes.
* [**00:08:12**] Why these fights for transparency matter, and why the American people deserve to see what the government has been withholding.
* [**00:10:26**] The bigger picture: this isn't only about Epstein. It's about whether wealth and power can shield people from accountability--and what we do about it.

There are still enormous unanswered questions surrounding Epstein, his associates, and what happened at Zorro Ranch. New Mexico is fighting for records. Katie Phang is fighting for transparency. Earlier this year, the Supreme Court delivered another ruling that undercuts the landmark 1965 Voting Rights Act.

Peter, in just a moment I’m going to tell you about the reality of running for governor as a Black man in the South.
But first, I need to ask: Will you chip in any amount you can right now to help me make history as South Carolina’s first Black governor? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jermaine-aug26?refcode=080726_1]
Early in my campaign, I was attending a Zoom chat with a group of supporters when someone wrote these words:
“Trump is going to remove you n****** soon its only a matter of freaking time. YOU STUPID BLACK N*****”
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jermaine-aug26?refcode=080726_1 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jermaine-aug26?refcode=080726_1]
I wish I could tell you I was shocked, but I wasn’t. This sentiment is all too familiar.
I’ve been told all my life to sit down and wait my turn. When I ran for the State Legislature, I was told I was too loud, too direct, and too Black to win - I didn’t listen, and I defeated a 22-year incumbent. Then, during my time in the Legislature, I watched my Republican colleagues, who claimed to be my friends, vote for racist policies.
Just like I stood up to my colleagues then, I’m not going to soften the truth now to make folks comfortable. Encountering racism is the reality of running to be the first Black governor of South Carolina. But we can’t let this hate decide whether people like me get to lead.
When they try to intimidate us into silence, that’s our cue to raise our voices even louder. The success of this campaign is going to come down to folks like you refusing to look away. I'm not backing down, and I need to know you're standing with me. Will you chip in anything you can right now? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jermaine-aug26?refcode=080726_1]

In the GOP primary debate, John Sununu told a roomful of Republicans he's running for Senate to send me back to "bussing tables" at my family's "chicken restaurant."

He meant it as an insult. As if the people who work in restaurants - who cook your food, clear your plates, keep family businesses that are the heart of our state alive - have something to be embarrassed about.

**I'm not embarrassed. I'm proud.**

My family opened our restaurant over 100 years ago. I know what a 65‐hour week feels like because I've worked one. I know what it means to show up every day, work hard, and treat the people around you like they matter - because they do.

**John Sununu has never had to work hard a day in his life.** He was born into the Sununu political dynasty. His family's "business" isn't a restaurant serving New Hampshire families. It owns a literal gold mine in Azerbaijan that sells minerals to China.

That's what John Sununu calls honest work.

New Hampshire workers deserve a senator who knows what a hard day's labor actually looks like - who fights for small business owners, for restaurant workers, for every family just trying to make ends meet. John Sununu is running to protect people like himself. **I'm running for everyone else.**

He showed us who he is with these elitist comments. Now let's make sure he doesn't represent us. Senate Republicans who refuse to fight for election integrity **DO NOT DESERVE OUR CAMPAIGN CONTRIBUTIONS**. There, we said it. Why should conservatives help these RINOs run their campaigns when they won't even try to secure their own elections? It makes no sense. **_No SAVE Act, no contributions. Period._** Thankfully, there's a group of Republicans who mean business. Let's call them **SAVE Act Conservatives**. I'm talking about Mike Lee (R-UT), Rick Scott (R-FL), and many others who not only claim to support the SAVE America Act but are also willing to do the hard work to pass it. For example, these leaders have gone on record opposing John Thune's plan to take an extended recess without forcing the Democrats to conduct a REAL talking filibuster of the SAVE America Act. Their message is clear: "No results, no recess." **THESE ARE THE LEADERS who deserve our support.** [**Please stand with these patriots who are running for election in 2026 by making a split contribution to their campaigns.**](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=7bdb747a60ec4ebc8de19aa0055fef04&_e=NzEYXiz1MD4SCV4y6mmhYthYB_GNSAxGlAGTyHB0h5rAPsqG0Su6G1A6hS-v_69poWb3y6BBBgKsAqYzRcbSh7jF2agAb-2rcEyeT7nA1Y3sn4FCQ5Efg3ensnrpsu4eUumCsFrB3CARYjSBaglub8xARlWgx9n51AWr77DEGSvPuxG5VswcyrdmrkHZLcl0wSdDT-20VtlGXU02YooM4SNR6o7bKJaEZikeDr2fUqU66crNvO5NOYyyHZsQhH9B1KcW9LjowuQvxeEQNo-t-jBNgCQLKWEhMKsjriVByb4TgtNagcWheBMFBxFmBxk70rqO7zhZSCFE-LZm8CEF2_V35WDVm4jOCSiDp-ze38zVoC22EFrzQzoM5XR6v0i8wV0jqC2BO--e8BuMTkeW4A%3D%3D) By funding the **SAVE Act Conservatives** , you can send a message to the RINO Establishment in Washington that they cannot ignore. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. And I'm glad to know that Landmark Legal Foundation is right there at my side. My friends at Landmark fight hard to save our country. Plus, in gratitude for your gift of $250 or more, Landmark will send you a copy of my latest book, On Power. I think you'll find it interesting. Your gift will help Landmark raise the $750,000 necessary to press ahead on all these fronts this year. The good thing about a donation to Landmark is that it's tax-deductible. I am also a donor to Landmark Legal Foundation, and I will continue to be. I hope you will join me. Landmark's president, Pete Hutchison, and I look forward to your response. God Bless, Mark Levin Chairman Emeritus Landmark Legal Foundation Landmark Legal Foundation is a 501(c)(3) Not For Profit Organization. All donations are tax-deductible.

| | | Friend, Thank you for your strong support in July. We want to be honest with you about what July looked like from our perspective. Sabato's Crystal Ball moved 14 races toward Democrats in a single update, but Texas Senate stayed put. Polling continues to show this race is neck and neck. One Silicon Valley billionaire wrote a $10 million check to James Talarico's super PAC. Democrats raised over $1.1 billion nationally in the first six months of this year alone. Everything was moving in the wrong direction. _And then the conservative grassroots did what conservatives do._ **You showed up. **You gave. You proved that this race is not going to be decided by billionaire checkbooks and coastal money. [1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

At the start of the 2026 election cycle, Justice Democrats knew we were
facing an existential crisis in the Democratic Party.

We can either choose to be a party that fights like hell for working
people, or we can surrender our country to corporate oligarchs, white
supremacists, and fascists.

This is a now-or-never moment, so we went big and endorsed 15 progressive
candidates running in primaries against Do-Nothing Democratic incumbents
or for open seats.

Our primary season is officially over, and here’s how we made out.

10 of our 15 endorsements won their primaries in 7 states spanning the
country.

With your support, we raised over $412,000 from more than 12,000 donations
— with an average gift of $34 — directly for their campaigns. We also
launched TV and digital ads in a number of these races to combat the
attack ads from AIPAC and corporate super PACs.

7 of our primary winners are all but guaranteed to head to Congress in
January:

* Rev. Frederick Douglass Haynes III (TX-30)
* Chris Rabb (PA-03)
* Dr. Adam Hamawy (NJ-12)
* Darializa Avila Chevalier (NY-13)
* Claire Valdez (NY-07)
* Melat Kiros (CO-01)
* Donavan McKinney (MI-13)

With 9 Justice Democrats currently serving in the U.S. House, that bloc
will grow to at least 16 next year. That means we’ll have more Justice
Democrats in Congress than ever before come 2027!

But we can turn that 16 into 19 this November by helping Mai Vang (CA-07),
Angela Gonzales-Torres (CA-34), and Justin J. Pearson (TN-09) win their
general election fights in November.

The bigger our bloc, the sooner we’ll start passing the bold policies
working people deserve: Medicare for All, a livable minimum wage, housing
for all, an end to U.S. funding for Israel’s genocide, a moratorium on
data centers, and so much more.

I have.

Peter,

I am done listening to people call this a “humanitarian issue.”

What happened under Biden at the southern border was not compassion.

**It was the calculated dismantling of national sovereignty and the people who ran it knew exactly what they were doing.**

Millions of illegal crossings. Gotaways who never got counted. Fentanyl poured into every community. Cartels treated the border like their own private highway. Cities and towns were forced to absorb the cost while the architects of the policy lived behind gates and security details.

**This was not incompetence. This was policy.**

Until Republicans came to power, our border was a mess. Now, we have record lows in crossings. But the Democrats are insistent that this is not the way.

They try to lecture us about “democracy” but are perfectly comfortable ignoring the most basic democratic principle of all: _that the people who live here get to decide who joins them._

They call enforcement “cruel.” They call open borders “justice.” They call you a bigot for noticing that the rule of law is being selectively applied, _and always against the people who actually follow it._

**I will not sit quietly and let these socialist Democrat radicals take power again and reinstitute the policies that led to the death of American citizens at the hands of illegals.**

I will not pretend it is accidental; Democrats know exactly what they’re doing.

If you still believe America has the right to exist as a sovereign nation with secure borders and enforceable laws, then this is the moment to act like it.

This is concerning, Peter.

Peter, Roy Cooper here. I’m worried.
We have less than three months left until Election Day, and unfortunately, we’re not where we need to be to reach our fundraising goals. [**_If you’re able to chip in today for the first time to help us get back on track, it would make a big impact and mean a lot to me._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1002&amount=5&t=9&akid=2559%2E124072%2EIBBFg2)
Here’s why it’s so important that we turn around our fundraising numbers:
North Carolina is where the fight for U.S. Senate control will be won or lost. Flipping this seat is a _must_ if we’re going to take back the majority, and that’s why the GOP is going all in to defeat me.
Republican super PACs are flooding this race with nearly $100 million so far to crush our momentum and prop up their handpicked MAGA candidate, former RNC chair Michael Whatley. President Trump is smearing my name to his millions of followers on social media. His buddy Stephen Miller even went on Fox News recently to rant and rave about me.
Their attacks are working: We’re getting outspent, and a recent poll of this race shows my narrow lead shrinking to just 4 points.
**If folks like you chip in and we hit our goals, we’ll be able to keep up with the GOP and ensure this race stays competitive. If we don’t meet our fundraising targets, we won’t.**
[**_That’s why this is so important, Peter, so I have to ask: Will you give $5 or whatever amount you can spare today to help us get back on track, flip North Carolina and take back the Senate majority?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1002&amount=5&t=10&akid=2559%2E124072%2EIBBFg2)

[**Change can happen in a generation. I know because it happened to me.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136933881/639076710/-1475871445?refcode=email_080926_bio-weeklydonor&amount=6&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhZDQ1NjMxNi0zMTk0LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_vfKu_0epcatkAMPX5fgYH8SR1Cp4OAjvupVJuWVhYg=)
When my dad was five years old, he immigrated from Mexico to Texas. He picked cotton and tomatoes in the fields of the Rio Grande Valley, all the while dreaming that one day he would work his way out of poverty and make it to the middle class.
My parents taught me the value of hard work. And I grew up believing that if we worked hard, _anything_ was possible.
But when I got to college, I realized my parents didn’t have the money to pay for my tuition and their groceries. So I worked all kinds of odd jobs to put myself through school. It took seven years, but I finished my degree and became the first person in my family to graduate from college.
When my daughter was born, I felt in my core the same determination that drove my parents: _there was nothing that would keep me from doing everything in my power to shape a stronger, more equitable future for Amelia and her generation._
**[I’m in this fight today because nothing will stop me from pursuing a better future for our children — and with this grassroots movement by my side, we’ve been able to make some incredible progress in Congress and in our community.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136933882/639076711/-1475871445?refcode=email_080926_bio-weeklydonor&amount=6&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhZDQ1NjMxNi0zMTk0LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_vfKu_0epcatkAMPX5fgYH8SR1Cp4OAjvupVJuWVhYg=) **

Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
CNN: Efforts to game the 2026 election intensify as Republicans draw new maps [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=080926_2&amount=25]
The immediate impact shows how partisan the Louisiana v. Callais case before the Supreme Court was, Team.
In the first week after this decision, five states moved to redraw their maps , dilute the impact of minority voters, and return parts of the country to a suppressive era we thought we left behind sixty years ago. Louisiana itself stopped an election with voting already in progress , and other states are moving to change their own maps soon.
CNN says this has created " an unprecedented amount of flux in American democracy six months before Election Day ." Candidates don’t know where to run. Lawmakers are seeing their districts carved up. Voters don’t know which district they live in.
This is all about power. Whether districts are fair or everyone is represented has been tossed by the wayside for MAGA's desperate grasp to control a country that's more disillusioned with their actions by the day.

Striking down the last remnants of the Voting Rights Act is exactly why the Supreme Court held this case over from last year. Gutting Section 2, which requires that racial minorities have an equal opportunity to meaningfully participate in the electoral process , is going to take us backwards in time and allow racial gerrymandering to be a standard practice, silencing more voters.
Long before the MAGA movement, Chief Justice Roberts saw the removal of the VRA as one of his top goals for his time on the Court. President Trump followed this decision with a directive for conservative-led states to erase multiple majority-Black districts across the South. His supporters are climbing over one another to comply.
The consequences are simple to understand and grave for voter participation. The harder we make it to vote, the more politicians make voter participation feel worthless, the less people actually take part. Needless to say, the less people who participate, the less our democracy and our government looks like the people it's supposed to represent.

📅 Weekly Update – August 9, 2026🏫 Touring the Arizona College of Nursing – Phoenix CampusOn Wednesday afternoon, I toured the Arizona College of Nursing – Phoenix campus, located right here in District 2. Arizona College of Nursing is a for‐profit, accredited institution offering an accelerated three‐year Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) program. It is one of several campuses the college operates across the country.The Phoenix campus serves students who are eager to enter the nursing workforce quickly, with a curriculum centered on clinical readiness and licensure preparation. Local healthcare partners provide hands‐on clinical training, giving students real‐world experience as they progress through the program. Graduates from this campus will hopefully help fill critical nursing positions and support efforts to address Arizona’s ongoing nursing shortage.In March 2026, the college earned accreditation from the American Nurses Credentialing Center for its continuing education programs. This recognition places the institution among a global network of accredited providers offering evidence‐based professional development for nurses.
🧬 Visit to Envita Medical CentersOn Friday, I had the opportunity to tour Envita Medical Centers in North Scottsdale with Dr. John Oertle. Envita provides customized, patient‐driven care, integrating advanced medical technologies and individualized treatment plans.Seeing how far medical innovation has come, giving me tremendous hope. Many people don’t know that my dad passed away in 2006 from pancreatic cancer in his early 60s, at a time when treatment options were extremely limited. Today, thanks to expanded research and new therapies, patients facing this devastating diagnosis have more options and more hope than ever before. I am grateful for the continued advancements in cancer care and the dedicated professionals working to improve outcomes for patients and families.📣 Campaign UpdateIf you live in District 2 and would like to request a yard sign, we would be happy to deliver one to you. Please [email me](mailto:info@bolickforarizona.com?subject=Deliver%20a%20Bolick%20yard%20sign&body=) and we will make it happen!If you’re interested in hosting a meet‐and‐greet, please reach out—these gatherings are a great way to connect with neighbors and discuss the issues that matter most to our community. Please [email me](mailto:info@bolickforarizona.com?subject=I'd%20like%20to%20host%20a%20meet%20and%20greet&body=) so we can get it scheduled!🤝 Volunteer OpportunitiesDo you have a few hours between now and the November election?I represent the most highly competitive State Senate district in Arizona, and your support can make a meaningful difference. Whether it’s canvassing, phone banking, or helping at events, we would love to have you on our volunteer team. Please [email me](mailto:info@bolickforarizona.com?subject=I'd%20like%20to%20volunteer%20to%20help%20hold%20the%20State%20Senate&body=) so we can pull together to protect this seat.📆 Upcoming EventsIn order to make the right investments to hold this highly competitive State Senate seat, we are continuing to hold fundraisers to raise the necessary resources to keep the GOP majority. You can help by making a donation, or inviting other potential donors to donate to help me.📍 August 19, 2026Fundraiser – Downtown Phoenix🕓 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM📩 [RSVP for the address.](mailto:info@bolickforarizona.com?subject=I%20want%20to%20support%20Shawnna%20on%208%2F19&body=)
📍 September 16, 2026Fundraiser – North Scottsdale🕠 4:30 PM to 6:30 PM📩 [RSVP for the address](mailto:info@bolickforarizona.com?subject=I%20want%20to%20help%20Shawnna%20on%209%2F16&body=).
Thank you for your continued support!Best,Shawnna

**TOP NEWS**
**“Musk, Abbott confirm $17B Terafab plant will be built near College Station”** via [Houston Chronicle](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Andrea Leinfelder** – It’s official: SpaceX and Tesla are building a massive $16.8 billion chipmaking facility outside of College Station in Grimes County.

SpaceX has been working on this deal for months and has already negotiated tens of millions of dollars in incentives with Grimes County , local school districts and the state for the advanced semiconductor facility, called Terafab.

The facility is expected to span 100 million square feet and employ more than 3,000 people. The initial phase of development is expected to cost $16.8 billion, SpaceX said Thursday , lower than the company’s prior estimates of $55 billion.

“We’re now embarking on the most epic chip-building effort,” **Elon Musk** , CEO of SpaceX and Tesla, said in a statement . “The Terafab is bringing cutting-edge manufacturing to America, creating thousands of high-paying jobs in the Lone Star State and enabling us to produce AI chips at scale for use on Earth and in space.” Gov. **Greg Abbott** announced Thursday that the project is receiving a $30 million Texas Enterprise Fund grant from the state. **Joe Fauth III** said in a statement. “When we can connect a company like SpaceX and the Terafab project to develop an industrial site in Grimes County, that makes all the sense in the world.” _(__[Houston Chronicle](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“New Texas data center projects frozen until state audits them”** via [The Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s**Paul Cobler** and **Alejandra Martinez** – Amid growing public backlash to the rapid buildout of data centers across Texas, Gov.**Greg Abbott** on Monday announced a moratorium on the approval of data centers until regulatory agencies can audit proposed data centers seeking connection to the state’s electric grid.

It is unclear how long the audit will take, but the effort is Abbott’s strongest effort yet to slow the development of these data centers statewide and underscores how little information members of the public, including state leaders, know about the facilities.

Abbott is asking the Public Utility Commission of Texas and the Electric Reliability Council of Texas to ensure data center developers provide information on tax breaks they will receive; power use and generation; water use and cooling operations; efforts to reduce impacts on local communities; and ownership of the facility. Any projects that fail Abbott’s ordered “comprehensive verification and audit” should be denied connection to the grid, the governor said.

“Our top priority is to protect Texans’ safety and quality of life,” Abbott wrote in a statement. “Any project that fails to comply with the requirements set forth by the PUCT and ERCOT, and by state law, must be denied connection to the Texas grid. Simply put, Texans must come first.” _(__[TX TRIB](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Report: More than half of Texas businesses have adopted AI”** via [KXAN Austin](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Cami Knott** – More than half of Texas businesses are already using artificial intelligence, according to a new report that argues the technology is rapidly becoming a part of everyday business operations across the state. The report was released Tuesday by Build American AI, a 501(c)(4) nonprofit advocacy organization that promotes U.S. leadership in artificial intelligence.

Citing the Dallas Federal Reserve’s Texas Business Outlook Survey, the report says 59.1% of surveyed Texas businesses reported using either traditional or generative AI in May 2025, up from 38.3% just a year earlier. Generative AI is also being adopted faster than past technologies. According to the Dallas Fed, it took just three years for generative AI to reach a 36% adoption rate among Texas Business Outlook Survey respondents.

The report argues AI is no longer primarily a tool for major technology companies. Instead, it says businesses across industries are using the technology to streamline routine tasks, from drafting contractor estimates and writing product descriptions to reducing paperwork in healthcare clinics and improving logistics operations. Small businesses are also increasingly embracing AI. Using U.S. Small Business Administration and U.S. Chamber of Commerce data, the report estimates roughly 1.86 million Texas small businesses already use an AI platform. _(__[KXAN](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Houston has seen nearly 3,000 layoffs this year. Here are the largest.”** via [Houston Chronicle](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Erica Grieder** – Nearly 20 companies in the Houston region laid off 2,697 employees during the first six months of the year, slightly more than the 2,440 workers who lost their jobs to layoffs during the same period last year, according to the Texas Workforce Commission.

But the Houston economy is beating economists’ expectations heading into the second half of the year, according to economists, with elevated oil prices boosting the region’s energy sector and consumers spending more on events such as the 2026 World Cup.

“Houston’s acceleration is all the more notable against a cooling national backdrop,” noted **Mohammad Ahmadizadeh** , economist and principal data analyst for Workforce Solutions Gulf Coast, Houston’s regional workforce development board, in a June report. _(__[HOU CHRON](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Why Texas is betting ‘Y’all Street’ can take on Wall Street”** via [NPR](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Maria Aspan** – Construction workers stand at the site of Goldman Sachs’ new campus in Dallas. The New York investment bank is supersizing its presence in the Texas city amid a financial boom. Local political leaders and the banking executives they’ve wooed are calling it "Y’all Street."

The New York investment bank plans to open this 800,000-square-foot campus in 2028, with space to eventually employ more than 5,000 local workers. The building will supersize Goldman’s presence in Dallas, where the company already has its second-largest U.S. office after its global headquarters in Manhattan.

Goldman is building its new campus in “the beating heart of Y’all Street,” says **Aasem Khalil** , the Goldman Sachs partner who runs its Dallas office. He rattles off the names of Goldman’s top U.S. competitors, like JPMorgan Chase and Morgan Stanley — both also headquartered in New York — and points out that they also have or are considering Dallas offices. _(__[NPR](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Kay Granger, first GOP woman from Texas to win House seat, dies at 83”** via [The Washington Post](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s**Anusha Mathur** –**Kay Granger** , a trailblazing Texas Republican who served as the first female mayor of Fort Worth and went on to spend 14 terms in Congress, rising to become the first woman from her party to chair the powerful House Appropriations Committee, has died. She was 83.

Her death was announced on social media Sunday by Speaker **Mike Johnson** and the House Republican Conference. Additional details were not immediately available. Ms. Granger’s family had announced in December 2024 that she had dementia, amid claims that her staff tried to conceal her cognitive decline.

A former teacher and small-business owner, Ms. Granger served for four years as mayor of Fort Worth before being elected to Congress in 1996. After becoming Appropriations chairwoman in 2019, she wielded immense influence over federal spending and helped steer funds toward Fort Worth-based defense companies such as Lockheed Martin and the helicopter-maker Bell Textron.

Ms. Granger did not seek reelection and left Capitol Hill in January 2025, at nearly 82. Just before her term ended, the Dallas Express, a conservative Texas media outlet, reported that she had not cast a vote in Congress in nearly five months. Her office continued issuing news releases and posting on social media according to the story, but reporters for the publication could not reach Ms. Granger’s aides, and her Texas office appeared closed. _(__[WAPO](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Kay Granger, trailblazing Fort Worth congresswoman, leaves lasting legacy”** via [Fort Worth Star-Telegram](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Eleanor Dearman** (summary produced with AI assistance) – **Kay Granger** , the first Republican woman to represent Texas in Congress and Fort Worth’s first female mayor, has reportedly died.

She retired in January after nearly three decades in the House, where she rose to chair the powerful Appropriations Committee.

The summary points above were compiled with the help of AI tools and edited by journalists.

The full story in the link at top was reported, written and edited entirely by journalists. _(__[FWST](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“San Antonio climber among 10 killed in Pakistan avalanche with famed mountaineer Nirmal Purja”** via [TPR](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Chris Arnold** – The celebrated climber Nirmal Purja and the nine other members of a mountaineering expedition group have died after they were caught in an avalanche on one of the highest peaks on earth.

“It is with profound sadness and immense heartbreak that we confirm that Mirmal ‘Nimsdai’ Purja tragically lost his life following the avalanche on Broad Peak,” Purja’s company Elite Expeditions said in a statement. Broad Peak is a 26,414 foot mountain in Northern Pakistan.

Purja, who was 43 years old and a British-Nepali climber, became world-renowned by breaking climbing records. In 2019, he was the first person to climb all 14 mountains world-wide with elevations above 8,000 meters (26,247 feet) in 6 months and 6 days. The feat was the subject of a Netflix feature documentary in 2021.

The American mountaineer was 39-year old **Mallory Geis** of San Antonio, Texas, according to the Associated Press. In a social media post earlier this year she wrote about her decision to close her Pilates studio to pursue high altitude climbing. “So here we go. Taking a giant leap of faith into the unknown to see where life goes. I have a sneaking suspicion there will be lots of helmets, harnesses, and crampons involved,” Geis posted. _(__[TPR](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Professors sue Texas A &M; System over limits on teaching race, gender”** via [The Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s Jessica Priest – Four professors and a national faculty group asked a federal judge Monday to block the Texas A&M University System’s restrictions on teaching about race, gender and sexuality and to reinstate courses canceled under the policy.

The university system bars professors from “advocating” race or gender ideology or topics related to sexual orientation or gender identity. The policy applies to all 12 universities in the system. It requires presidential approval to address those subjects in certain courses and, according to the lawsuit, prohibits them in core courses.

The lawsuit asks the judge to rescind instructions requiring professors to remove particular readings or subjects and declare the policy unconstitutional. The professors and faculty group allege the restrictions violate the professors’ First Amendment rights and are so vague that faculty cannot determine what they may teach without risking discipline. They want the judge to restore courses removed from the core curriculum and prevent the regents from imposing similar restrictions.

The American Association of University Professors brought the lawsuit alongside four professors: Texas A&M; professors **Leonard Bright** , **Vanita Reddy** and **Landon Sadler** and Tarleton State University professor **Aaron George**. They are represented by the ACLU of Texas, the national ACLU and the Houston law firm Yetter Coleman. They sued the system’s regents in federal court in Houston. _(__[TX TRIB](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_
|
---
**2026**
**“James Talarico rolls out “New American Dream” economic plan”** via [The Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s**Kayla Guo** , **Gabby Birenbaum** and **Colleen DeGuzman** – Democratic U.S. Senate nominee**James Talarico** proposed a sweeping economic agenda on Wednesday that called for repealing recent GOP tax cuts for the wealthy and enacting universal childcare, among other policies meant to lower everyday costs.

“We have an affordability crisis because we have a corruption crisis,” Talarico said during a nearly 30-minute speech to an audience of 1,300 people in Arlington. “For too many of our neighbors — for too many Texans — the American dream has become an American nightmare.”

Throughout his campaign, Talarico has stuck to a populist economic message that links rising costs to billionaire political influence and an economy he says is tilted in favor of the ultrawealthy over working people. Wednesday’s address kicked off a monthlong tour to promote his first detailed rollout of his proposals to reverse course, under the banner of what he is calling the “New American Dream.” _(__[TX TRIB](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Texas ban on several THC products emerges as potential wedge issue in Senate race”** via [Houston Public Media](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s**Andrew Schneider** – A recent Texas state ban on several forms of tetrahydrocannabinol or THC, the main intoxicating component in cannabis, is already becoming an issue in this year’s U.S. Senate election.

The ban took effect Friday. State Rep. **James Talarico** , the Democratic Senate nominee, called the ban “a gift to the cartels” in a Monday statement and said the state is “going back to the days of prohibition” seven years after the Texas Legislature legalized hemp.

The ban is a result of a Texas Supreme Court ruling earlier this year that permits the state’s Department of State Health Services (DSHS) to reclassify most types of hemp-derived THC as a schedule I drug, making it illegal to sell and possess in the state. DSHS had been blocked from making the reclassification by a court injunction issued in 2021. Since then, different kinds of THC could be sold by businesses in the state. _(__[Houston Public Media](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Democrat Gina Hinojosa makes big ad buy in effort to unseat GOP Gov. Greg Abbott”** via [Dallas Morning News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘ **Karen Brooks Harper** – A new $340,000 ad campaign by **Gina Hinojosa** , the Democrat trying to unseat Texas Gov. **Greg Abbott** , dropped on Tuesday in markets across the state – ramping up her battle against the Republican running for a historic fourth term in Austin.

The campaign is targeting Dallas-Fort Worth voters. The 30- and 60-second ads, featuring a diverse group of Hinojosa supporters, promise to rein in Republican leaders “who forgot who they serve.” The ads carry on the theme of fighting corporate interests the state lawmaker says have been controlling the Texas GOP for far too long.

“Greg Abbott had one job – take care of Texas,” supporters say in one ad. “Instead, he took care of his billionaire donors.” The cable ad buy brings Hinojosa’s campaign spending to nearly $1 million, according to a spokesperson. The ads will continue across the state until the Nov. 6 election.

Hinojosa had about $3 million in her campaign account as of June 30. By contrast, Abbott had just over $67 million. Hinojosa and other prominent Democrats on the ticket have campaigned on a theme of the wealthy heavily influencing state government to the detriment of Texans — referring to private school vouchers, high property taxes, struggling hospitals and the encroachment of big data centers. _(__[DMN](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“In Texas, a political group bets $6 million on Latino voters coming back to Democrats”** via [Houston Chronicle](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s**Jonathan J. Cooper** – A left-leaning group is planning to spend $6 million organizing Latino voters in Texas, a group that has trended away from Democrats but is pivotal to their hopes of picking up seats in Congress.

Somos Votantes has started a $2 million statewide voter education push centered on door-to-door conversations and voter registration. Its affiliated political committee, Somos PAC, is preparing a $4 million advertising campaign focused on three South Texas House districts, where they aim to channel voter angst about the economy into support for Democratic candidates in Republican-leaning districts.

“We’re really hoping that we can reconsolidate support for Democrats by presenting the positive economic vision that Democratic candidates in these House districts have,” said **Melissa Morales** , the founder of Somos Votantes.

Texas is at the crossroads of the fight for control of the U.S. House in the November midterms, and winning back Hispanics who were drawn to President **Donald Trump** in 2024 will be key to Democrats’ chances there. _(__[HOU CHRON](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_
|
---
**STATE GOVERNMENT**
**“Data centers use lots of water and power, but Texas officials don’t know exactly how much”** via [TPR](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Kailey Hunt** –**Torrie Martin’s** ranch is located near the Vistra Hays Power Plant, which generates around 990 megawatts of power, enough to power 250,000 homes. The proximity to the power station makes Martin’s neighborhood a desirable place to build data centers. Data centers need a lot of power to operate, and, depending on how they’re cooled, a lot of water too.

As more and more data center developers submit proposals to build in Texas, questions about how they’ll impact Texas’ grid and contribute to drought conditions across the state are widespread. So much so, that Gov. **Greg Abbott** effectively ordered a pause on all data center projects looking to connect to the grid until officials get a better grasp on the amount of resources they will use.

**Margaret Cook** , the vice president of water and community resilience for the Houston Advanced Research Center, said there is an answer to how much water data centers are using. “The clear answer to the general question is it depends,” she said. Cook said it depends primarily on two things: how big a data center is and what cooling technology it uses. _(__[TPR](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“More than 85,000 students using school vouchers in Texas’ first year”** via [The Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s**Jaden Edison** and **Sneha Dey** – More than 85,000 families are participating in Texas’ private school voucher program during its first year, a number that could increase as state officials finalize enrollment data, according to a new state report.

White families make up the largest share of participants so far, as do those considered low-income, the comptroller’s office noted in the report released Monday. The report did not say how many students previously attended private school or received home schooling, although earlier data showed that 57% of families invited to the program fell into that category.

While it appears unlikely that the majority of first-year voucher recipients will come from public schools, the largest numbers of participating families live within the boundaries of some of the state’s most populous districts — with Houston, Dallas and Northside in the San Antonio area leading the way. _(__[TX TRIB](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_
|
---
**#TXLEGE**
**“Texas governor’s data center moratorium prompts calls for special legislative session”** via [Houston Public Media](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s**Natalie Weber** – Critics say the governor must call legislators to Austin to pass state laws regulating data centers.

After Texas Gov. **Greg Abbott** declared a moratorium on new data centers, pending a state-led audit of these fast-emerging and controversial facilities, several of his political opponents issued statements critiquing his actions.

But they weren’t criticizing his decision to temporarily prevent new data centers from connecting to the Texas power grid. Instead, they said Abbott’s actions didn’t go far enough. “Let’s be very clear about this: Abbott can take action now to end the data center madness,” Austin state Rep. **Gina Hinojosa** , the Democratic nominee for governor, said in a statement.

Texas Agriculture Commissioner **Sid Miller** , a Republican, was among critics calling for a special session. Abbott endorsed Miller’s opponent, **Nate Sheets** , who defeated Miller in this year’s GOP primary election. “Without legislative action, this directive is all hat and no cattle — empty political rhetoric wrapped in meaningless fluff,” Miller said in a statement. _(__[Houston Public Media](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Governor doesn’t want CPS Energy to be sole San Antonio electric provider”** via [San Antonio Express-News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Molly Smith** , **Kelsey Brown** and **Megan Rodriguez** – Gov. **Greg Abbott** said he wants to break up CPS Energy’s monopoly in San Antonio and give customers a choice of electricity providers — a move that could potentially cut into the city-owned utility’s revenue and hurt city finances.

Abbott pitched his plan to eliminate the “city monopolies” on electricity on Tuesday. It’s largely aimed at San Antonio and Austin, which own their electric and water utilities.

He said he’ll ask lawmakers to take up his proposal in the 2027 Texas Legislature. The governor’s office said San Antonio customers would save up to 13% on their monthly energy bills if CPS had competition.

**Editorial: “Texas’ anti-NIMBY housing law is getting results”** via [Dallas Morning New](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)s – When the Texas Legislature passed Senate Bill 840, the goal was to boost the state’s housing stock in major cities. The law allows developers to build multifamily and mixed-use projects in districts zoned for commercial use without having to request a zoning change.

Many cities have been howling in protest since. Some have put up new rules to undermine SB 840. But even with those obstacles, SB 840 appears to be working. Since the law went into effect in September, it has directly facilitated more than 1,250 housing units and indirectly supported at least 7,235 units, according to a report by a bipartisan coalition that backs the law.

The nearly 8,500 homes that have been enabled by SB 840 are not all a done deal. Some have been approved, and others are pending. But one thing is clear: Developers want to build this housing. The coalition that authored the report — Texas Appleseed, the American Enterprise Institute and Texans for Reasonable Solutions — identified multifamily applications that would not have been allowed before SB 840 and other projects whose rezoning was made easier by the law. _(__[DMN](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

**“Following ban, Texas hemp reps sue state for violating commerce protections”** via [The Texas Tribune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s **Stephen Simpson** – Three members of the hemp industry are suing the state of Texas for violating commerce protections after it was announced last week that nearly all hemp-derived THC products are illegal.

On Friday, two hemp retailers and a distributor filed a lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas against the Texas Department of State Health Services; Attorney General **Ken Paxton** ; and the Galveston County criminal district attorney and sheriff, alleging that classifying hemp-derived substances as illegal violates the 2018 Farm Bill, which removed it from the federal Controlled Substances Act.

The complaint states that the reinstated definitions provide no delineation between lawful hemp and unlawful marijuana; that it’s preempted by the 2018 Farm Bill’s protections for the interstate hemp market; and that these classifications impose an unconstitutional burden on interstate commerce.

“For more than seven years, Texans have built a multibillion-dollar hemp industry under laws that define these products as legal hemp. **“AI is breaking out of Silicon Valley’s control. Will Ted Cruz care?”** via [Houston Chronicle](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)‘s**J.B. Branch** – Sen. **Ted Cruz** has spent years insisting that the greatest threat to artificial intelligence is regulating it. Cruz believes the companies building the world’s most powerful AI systems should be allowed to experiment on their own and self-regulate. He believes so deeply in this philosophy that he named his signature AI bill after it, the SANDBOX Act.

Today, that name has become an uncomfortable reminder of how spectacularly wrong his approach has been. To understand why, it helps to understand what a “sandbox” actually is. In AI, a sandbox is an isolated digital environment where developers can push an AI system to its limits without letting it interact with the real world. If something goes wrong, the damage is supposed to stay inside the sandbox. Cruz’s SANDBOX Act is grounded in that thinking. Give AI companies freedom to experiment, exemptions from laws they choose, and trust that sandboxes will keep the public safe.

That premise has not aged well. In just the past two weeks, two companies widely regarded as leaders in AI — OpenAI and Anthropic — have acknowledged security failures involving the very sandboxes meant to contain their systems. OpenAI relaxed safety protocols, and one of its most advanced AI models carried out cyberattacks against Hugging Face, one of the most prominent open-source platforms. OpenAI did not know about the incident for days.

Days after OpenAI’s announcement, Anthropic announced that it had discovered something equally alarming. The company disclosed that their advanced model had breached their sandbox resulting in hacks into three organizations. Neither Anthropic nor the affected organizations even realized the intrusions had occurred until months later. Both companies described the incidents as unprecedented. Ultimately, both had to rely on a Chinese open source model to fix the cybersecurity patch. That means that ironically, the same Chinese open source models that Ted Cruz has lambasted as a threat to American AI innovation actually helped stop one of the most alarming AI cybersecurity incidents to date. _(__[HOU CHRON](https://link.mail.beehiiv.)_ _)_

It starts tomorrow. According to media reservations, Mike Lawler is going to air his first TV ads of 2026 starting tomorrow. From now until November, he going to spend whatever he can to dominate the airwaves. [Can you please make your first donation to Cait Conley’s campaign in NY-17, to help us push back? Anything you can give makes a major difference.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqiBIysd_1t7dQL51NYrcy9WUmGFTC9n4qFGNrnI9QqPxLAVBD8-1--qq1w00JA6gD3VcF_-LrM3nFTbPOLtPAUxIj80z0vE4ViWeNwpUsMjewUYOgO6vWiubBMlV8pSgkjkPkDPwL8alvWQebCAO0NDieBxi0PdemnRs08tVGi3sc7gBcl5RbgEqWytjtjYS5sRJAH3IEC9tTAKwl0OHTeFsS6GlPpCLvoHRfELfIc4itMrLtBTSp7XxSqFvXqoecXf7XNSnrnyIIy70HeVy4ygeMsM3sYMGkIdMIrqVk2lfjoAS_NztSA06woF7wi_aJ0Ymym3y7RLGRJk9ncrYY/4t1/U7OTz0bITcysOAFwILbfZw/h0/h001.RpaOuULALCcQGPnDMFNHWYCNx3PTOoSy3EbwaSQY4bo) | [DONATE »](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqiBIysd_1t7dQL51NYrcy9WUmGFTC9n4qFGNrnI9QqPxLAVBD8-1--qq1w00JA6gD3VcF_-LrM3nFTbPOLtPAQhghunl36nxGVS4EwqT-REZhTK6nBbrLZHtK12KajF4nQvKoNy3iM1BjngWpmDypXqWwT03m55F1HLljVKc2Qv2xJhqOsU8XZDZtEGHO2aQGCfhQQ10aiqmTtI05GHZ-bAo83DOiG5VkUjJajjYZbDPDW2QgYi5rGR_-LcXEvC6EwArmc6VwYoTbvbBEDFEdI-JSy0g3Zk8htcBqZgaVkSS4NC6xMboasAhcatKYdB-LwMxC576GVXZVdA6h2UNA/4t1/U7OTz0bITcysOAFwILbfZw/h1/h001.Paf39vzVnAV_1g5D9p4ODR1eMSRhUgWs9Uh4w4Urboo)

The simple truth is we are not going to be able to outspend Mike Lawler. He and his MAGA allies are going to have more money than we will.
But that just means that we have to run a smarter campaign.
So our team is going over our budget with a fine tooth comb, looking for the most effective ways to spend our budget. It’s working so far. Political experts just upgraded us from Lean-R to Tossup — but Lawler’s early ad spending is exactly the type of thing that could wipe out all of our progress.
That’s why we’re coming to you.
If everyone reading this email donated just $17 or $10, we would have the resources to build a competitive voter outreach organization and take on Lawler’s machine.
But the harsh truth is, not everyone gives.

We write as friends of the court, because how it is decided will decide how our own ballots are handled. We believe that **only American citizens should cast ballots in American elections** , and that confirming citizenship before a ballot is mailed is a reasonable step, not a radical one. Twenty-three states and the District of Columbia went to court to stop that verification from happening. A district judge blocked it on June 25. A divided appeals panel agreed. The question now before this Court is whether it may take effect while the case is argued. We respectfully ask the Court to allow it.
